# 🔒 Sub-Project → GDPR Compliance - Recruitify

**Parent Project**: [[PT Ai Recruitment Jobs]]
**Compliance Framework**: Isle of Man Applied GDPR
**Version**: 4.1 (Value-Optimised)

---

## 📄 Original GDPR Requirements Brief

**Recruitify Platform – GDPR-Compliant Developer Build Brief (v4.1, Value-Optimised)**

### Developer Executive Summary
Build the Recruitify platform with the following privacy-by-default standards:
- Two user roles (Candidate, Employer) with strict data separation.
- Static Terms & Privacy Policy accepted via checkbox at sign-up (timestamp logged).
- "Delete My Account" function with permanent deletion and audit logging.
- Automated data retention rules:
	  - Candidate accounts: delete after 36 months of inactivity
	  - Job applications: delete after 18 months of job closure
	  - Job postings: delete after 24 months of expiry
	  - Employer & financial data: retain 7 years for legal compliance
- Host all systems and backups in the UK or Isle of Man only.
- Generate a weekly anonymised analytics export (non-personal data only) to support product improvement.
- Secure all data with HTTPS, hashed passwords, and role-based access control.
- Manual handling of access/deletion requests via privacy@recruitify.im.

This implementation provides full compliance with the Isle of Man's Applied GDPR while maintaining a strong data governance and privacy framework.

### 1️⃣ User Roles & Account Basics
- Two account types: Candidate and Employer.
- Each registers with email + password.
- Employers can view only their own applicants.
- Admin access limited to authorised Recruitify staff.
- All connections via HTTPS; passwords hashed (bcrypt / argon2).

### 2️⃣ Privacy Policy & Terms
- Display checkbox at registration: 'I agree to Recruitify's Terms and Privacy Policy.'
- Store user ID, timestamp, IP address, and policy version.
- Publish static pages for Terms and Privacy Policy (footer links).
- Use a single standard privacy model (no opt-in toggles).
- Policy content must include controller identity, processing purposes, retention schedule, data rights, storage region, analytics use, and contact email (privacy@recruitify.im).

### 3️⃣ Account Deletion - Candidate
- Add 'Delete My Account' button in user settings.
- Permanently removes personal data, CVs, and related records.
- Log user ID + timestamp in deletion log.
- Automated cron job runs monthly to enforce retention rules.

### 4️⃣ Data Retention Schedule (Value-Optimised)

| Data Category | Retention Period | Purpose / Rationale |
|---------------|------------------|---------------------|
| Active Candidate Accounts | While active | Service delivery |
| Inactive Candidate Accounts | 36 months after last login | Typical job-seek cycles; allows re-engagement |
| Job Applications / CVs | 18 months after job closure | Analytics + dispute buffer |
| Employer Accounts | 7 years after closure | Business / tax records |
| Job Postings | 24 months after expiry | Market trend analytics |
| Usage Logs / Metrics | 24 months, then aggregated | Product improvement |
| Anonymised Analytics Data | Indefinite | Not personal data |
| Support Tickets / Messages | 12 months after resolution | Low value beyond this |
| Financial & Contract Records | 7 years | Accounting law |
| Marketing Consent Logs | Until withdrawal + 24 months | Evidence of lawful marketing |

### 5️⃣ Data Analytics / Service Improvement
- Create secondary anonymised dataset (analytics_jobs table) with only non-identifiable fields such as sector, skills, salary band, region, experience level, job type.
- Exclude names, emails, phone numbers, employer names, and IDs.
- Randomise IDs and update dataset daily/weekly via export script.
- Add boolean field 'allow_analytics' (default TRUE) for admin-managed opt-out.
- Retain anonymised data indefinitely.
- Include in Privacy Policy: 'Recruitify Limited may analyse anonymised or aggregated data to improve its services and understand employment trends. This analysis never identifies individual users.'

### 6️⃣ Security Controls
- HTTPS everywhere; secure cookies + CSP headers.
- Role-based access (Candidate / Employer / Admin).
- Encrypted database at rest.
- 2FA optional for employers; required for Admins.
- Secure password reset with token + expiry.
- Encrypted backups stored in UK / IOM.
- No production PII in test environments.
- Audit log for key actions – create, login, delete, export.

### 7️⃣ Data Storage & Hosting
- Host all systems and data in UK or Isle of Man regions (e.g. AWS London).
- Use UK / EU-based vendors for email, storage, analytics.
- No transfers outside these regions without Standard Contractual Clauses.
- Maintain a simple vendor register (name + region).

### 8️⃣ Data Subject Rights (Manual Process)
- Deletion via in-platform 'Delete Account'.
- Correction: users can edit their profiles.
- Access requests handled manually via privacy@recruitify.im within 30 days.
- Objections/restrictions handled by admin setting 'allow_analytics = FALSE'.
- Maintain internal log of all data requests and responses.

### 9️⃣ Breach & Audit Logging
- Log account creation, deletion, and admin views.
- Admin can export logs as CSV.
- Data breach process handled manually; record details and actions in an internal register.

### 🔟 AI Matching (Assistive-Only Phase 1)
- Matching algorithm provides recommendations only; no automated rejections.
- Add privacy statement: 'Recruitify uses automated tools to suggest suitable candidates or jobs based on skills and experience. All hiring decisions remain human-led.'

---

## 📋 Executive Summary

This sub-project implements full GDPR compliance for the Recruitify platform, ensuring privacy-by-default standards with:
- Two user roles (Candidate, Employer) with strict data separation
- Automated data retention with 9 different schedules
- UK/Isle of Man-only data hosting
- Privacy Policy & Terms acceptance tracking
- Self-service account deletion
- Weekly anonymised analytics exports
- Comprehensive security controls & audit logging

---

## ✅ Implementation Tasks

### 1️⃣ User Roles & Account Basics (8 Tasks)

#### Task 1.1: Implement Two-Tier User Account System
**Description**: Create separate account types for Candidate and Employer with role-based access control
**Technical Specs**:
- Database schema with `user_type` enum: ['candidate', 'employer', 'admin']
- Role-based middleware for route protection
- Separate registration flows for each role
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [x] Users can register as either Candidate or Employer ✅ 2025-11-07
- [x] Employers can only view their own job applications ✅ 2025-11-07
- [ ] Role is immutable after account creation
**Complexity**: Medium
**References**: Django User model with custom AbstractUser

---

#### Task 1.2: Email + Password Authentication
**Description**: Implement secure email/password authentication system
**Technical Specs**:
- Email validation (RFC 5322 compliant)
- Password requirements: min 12 chars, uppercase, lowercase, number, special char
- Rate limiting on login attempts (5 attempts per 15 min)
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Users register with valid email format
- [ ] Passwords meet security requirements
- [ ] Failed login attempts are rate-limited
**Complexity**: Low
**References**: Django authentication system

---

#### Task 1.3: Employer-Only Applicant Access
**Description**: Ensure employers can only access applicants for their own job postings
**Technical Specs**:
- Database queries filtered by `employer_id`
- Authorization checks before displaying applicant data
- Audit log for applicant profile views
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [x] Employers see only their applicants ✅ 2025-11-07
- [x] Direct URL access to other applicants is blocked ✅ 2025-11-07
- [ ] All applicant views are logged
**Complexity**: Medium
**References**: Django ORM query filtering

---

#### Task 1.4: Admin Access Controls
**Description**: Restrict admin access to authorised Recruitify staff only
**Technical Specs**:
- Separate admin user table with approval workflow
- IP whitelist for admin panel access (optional)
- Admin activity audit log
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Only approved staff can access admin panel
- [ ] All admin actions are logged with timestamp
- [ ] Regular users cannot escalate to admin
**Complexity**: Medium
**References**: Django admin with custom permissions

---

#### Task 1.5: HTTPS Enforcement
**Description**: Enforce HTTPS for all connections
**Technical Specs**:
- HTTPS redirect middleware (HTTP → HTTPS 301)
- HSTS header: `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`
- Secure cookie flags: `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] All HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS
- [ ] HSTS header present on all responses
- [ ] Cookies have secure flags set
**Complexity**: Low
**References**: Django SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT setting

---

#### Task 1.6: Password Hashing with bcrypt/argon2
**Description**: Implement secure password hashing
**Technical Specs**:
- Use argon2id algorithm (preferred) or bcrypt
- Salt rounds: 12 (bcrypt) or equivalent (argon2)
- Password rehashing on login if algorithm upgraded
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Passwords never stored in plaintext
- [ ] Hash algorithm is argon2id or bcrypt
- [ ] Old hashes auto-upgraded on user login
**Complexity**: Low
**References**: Django PASSWORD_HASHERS setting

---

#### Task 1.7: Database Foreign Key Constraints
**Description**: Ensure data integrity with proper relationships
**Technical Specs**:
- Foreign keys: `applications.employer_id` → `users.id`
- Foreign keys: `applications.candidate_id` → `users.id`
- Foreign keys: `job_postings.employer_id` → `users.id`
- ON DELETE CASCADE for user deletion
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] All relationships have foreign key constraints
- [ ] Orphaned records are prevented
- [ ] Cascade deletes work correctly
**Complexity**: Low
**References**: Django models with ForeignKey

---

#### Task 1.8: Session Management & Timeout
**Description**: Implement secure session handling
**Technical Specs**:
- Session timeout: 30 minutes idle, 8 hours absolute
- Session invalidation on password change
- Secure session storage (database-backed)
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Inactive sessions expire after 30 minutes
- [ ] Users logged out after 8 hours
- [ ] Password change invalidates all sessions
**Complexity**: Low
**References**: Django SESSION_COOKIE_AGE

---

### 2️⃣ Privacy Policy & Terms (7 Tasks)

#### Task 2.1: Create Privacy Policy Page
**Description**: Write and publish static Privacy Policy page
**Technical Specs**:
- Markdown/HTML static page at `/privacy-policy`
- Version number in URL: `/privacy-policy/v1.0`
- Include required sections:
  - Controller identity (Recruitify Limited)
  - Processing purposes
  - Retention schedule
  - Data subject rights
  - Storage region (UK/IOM)
  - Analytics use
  - Contact: privacy@recruitify.im
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Page accessible at `/privacy-policy`
- [ ] All required sections present
- [ ] Footer link to policy exists
**Complexity**: Low
**References**: Template from legal advisor

**Description**: Write and publish static Terms of Service page

- Static page at `/terms-of-service`

- Include: service description, user obligations, liability limits, termination
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Page accessible at `/terms-of-service`
- [ ] Footer link to terms exists
- [ ] Terms cover all required legal aspects
**Complexity**: Low
**References**: Template from legal advisor

---

#### Task 2.3: Registration Consent Checkbox
**Description**: Add consent checkbox to registration form
**Technical Specs**:
- Checkbox: "I agree to Recruitify's Terms and Privacy Policy"
- Links to both policies (open in new tab)
- Checkbox must be checked to proceed

#### Task 3.1: "Delete My Account" Button in Settings

#### Task 3.2: Account Deletion API Endpoint
**Description**: Create API endpoint to delete user account

#### Task 3.3: Deletion Audit Log
**Description**: Log all account deletions for audit trail
**Technical Specs**:
- Table: `deletion_log`

# Project Kickoff Workflow

**Purpose**: Properly initiate a new project with complete structure, connections, and context

**Triggers**: "start new project [name]", "project kickoff", "new project"

**Duration**: ~15-20 minutes

**When to use**: Beginning any new PT (Primary Thing) or OPT (Other Priority Thing) project

---

## Workflow Steps

### 1. Create Project Note
**Skill**: `obsidian-project-note`

**Actions**:
- Create new project note in appropriate location:
  - **High focus** → `3 Efforts/ON/[PT/OPT] - [Project Name].md`
  - **Active work** → `3 Efforts/3 Projects/[PT/OPT] - [Project Name].md`
  - **Ongoing** → `3 Efforts/Ongoing/[Project Name].md`
- Initialize with standard template:
  - YAML frontmatter (tags, dates, status)
  - Project overview and purpose
  - Goals & success criteria
  - Key stakeholders
  - Milestones & timeline
  - Resources & references
  - Log section for updates

**Output**: Structured project note ready for development

---

### 2. Link to Relevant People
**Skill**: `obsidian-persons`

**Actions**:
- Identify project stakeholders:
  - **Owner/Lead** (you or someone else)
  - **Collaborators** (working directly on project)
  - **Stakeholders** (interested parties, decision makers)
  - **Clients** (if client-facing)
- For each person:
  - Link in project note: `[[Person Name]]`
  - Update person note: Add project to their note
  - Update `Atlas Dots/Lists/People - Active Projects.md`
  - Assess relationship tier (may influence engagement)
- Create bidirectional links (project ← → person)

**Output**: People connections established

---

### 3. Add to Appropriate MOC
**Skill**: `obsidian-mocs`

**Actions**:
- Identify relevant Map of Content:
  - Business projects → `[[Atlas Maps/Business/]]`
  - Tech projects → `[[Atlas Maps/Tech/]]`
  - Personal projects → `[[Atlas Maps/Personal/]]`
  - Create new MOC if needed (e.g., "LLM Research Projects")
- Add project to MOC with brief description
- Add MOC link to project note
- Consider sub-MOCs for related projects

**Output**: Project organized in knowledge graph

---

### 4. Set Up Recurring Tasks & Milestones
**Skills**: Project note structure, task management

**Actions**:
- Define recurring tasks:
  - Weekly project updates (every Friday)
  - Regular syncs with collaborators (schedule)
  - Monthly progress reviews
  - Quarterly goal check-ins
- Set key milestones:
  - Project phases (Planning, Execution, Completion)
  - Deliverable dates
  - Review/feedback points
  - Go-live or ship dates
- Add to appropriate tracking:
  - Daily note queries (next actions)
  - Weekly review prompts
  - Calendar integration (if date-specific)

**Output**: Task structure and timeline in place

---

### 5. Define Success Criteria & Metrics
**Skills**: Strategic thinking, project planning

**Actions**:
- Articulate clear success criteria:
  - **What "done" looks like** (completion definition)
  - **Quality standards** (acceptance criteria)
  - **Impact measures** (how you'll know it worked)
- Set tracking metrics:
  - Progress indicators (% complete, milestones hit)
  - Quality metrics (bugs, feedback scores)
  - Business metrics (usage, revenue, engagement)
- Document in project note under "Goals & Success Criteria"

**Output**: Clear definition of success

---

### 6. Gather & Link Resources
**Skills**: Resource organization, reference management

**Actions**:
- Identify and link key resources:
  - **Documentation** (specs, requirements, PRDs)
  - **Research** (background reading, prior art)
  - **Tools** (software, templates, workflows)
  - **References** (similar projects, examples)
- Create links in project note:
  - Internal links to other notes
  - External URLs (with descriptions)
  - File attachments (if in vault)
- Consider creating supporting notes:
  - Research summary note
  - Technical architecture note
  - Meeting notes from kickoff

**Output**: Resources centralized and accessible

---

### 7. First Project Update
**Skill**: `obsidian-update-project`

**Actions**:
- Add initial log entry:
  - Today's date
  - Project kickoff completed
  - Initial thoughts/context
  - First next actions identified
  - Any immediate blockers/questions
- This establishes update pattern for future

**Output**: Project log started

---

## Expected Output Format

### Project Note Example
```markdown
---
tags:
  - type/project
  - status/active
  - focus/pt
  - category/tech
created: 2025-11-09, 17:00
modified: 2025-11-09
status: Active - Planning
progress: 5%
priority: ON
---

# PT - LLM Research Pipeline

## Overview
**Purpose**: Build comprehensive LLM research pipeline for DOME USA, enabling systematic evaluation and optimization of language models.

**Why this matters**: Critical infrastructure for client delivery, competitive advantage, knowledge building.

**Time allocation**: 35% (Primary Thing status)

## Goals & Success Criteria

### Primary Goals
1. Functional LLM evaluation pipeline (end-to-end)
2. Comprehensive documentation for team use
3. Initial POC with real client data

### Success Criteria
- ✅ Pipeline processes 100+ prompts/hour
- ✅ Results reproducible and traceable
- ✅ Documentation enables team self-service
- ✅ Client feedback positive (8/10+)

### Metrics
- **Progress**: Milestones completed / total
- **Quality**: Test coverage, error rate
- **Impact**: Client usage, feedback scores

## People & Stakeholders

### Project Team
- **Lead**: [[Natie Rautenbach]] (architect & implementer)
- **Collaborator**: [[Robert Pratt]] (LLM/RAG expertise, advisor)

### Stakeholders
- **Client**: [[Michael Cosgrave]] (product owner, strategy)
- **End Users**: DOME USA team

## Milestones & Timeline

**Phase 1: Architecture & Planning** (Weeks 1-2)
- [x] Project kickoff - 2025-11-09
- [ ] Architecture design review with Robert
- [ ] Technical spec documentation
- [ ] Tool selection finalized

**Phase 2: Core Development** (Weeks 3-6)
- [ ] Pipeline infrastructure built
- [ ] Evaluation metrics implemented
- [ ] Initial testing framework

**Phase 3: POC & Delivery** (Weeks 7-8)
- [ ] POC with client data
- [ ] Documentation completion
- [ ] Team training & handoff

**Target Completion**: End of December 2025

## Resources & References

### Documentation
- [[LLM Evaluation Frameworks]] - Research summary
- [[DOME USA - Technical Requirements]]
- [[Atlas Maps/Tech/LLM & AI Systems]] - MOC

### External Resources
- [LangChain Evaluation](https://docs.langchain.com/evaluation) - Framework reference
- [OpenAI Evals](https://github.com/openai/evals) - Inspiration

### Tools
- Python + uv (package management)
- LangChain (framework)
- Vector DB (selection pending)

## Current Status
**Status**: Active - Planning phase
**Progress**: 5% (kickoff complete, architecture in progress)
**Next Actions**:
1. Schedule architecture review with Robert (this week)
2. Research vector DB options (by Friday)
3. Draft technical spec outline (next week)

**Blockers**: None currently

## Log

### 2025-11-09, 17:00 - Project Kickoff
Project officially initiated. Completed:
- Project note structure created
- People connections established (Robert, Michael)
- Added to [[Atlas Maps/Tech/LLM & AI Systems]] MOC
- Milestones and timeline defined
- First next actions identified

Initial thoughts: Excited about building this infrastructure. Key success factor will be keeping it simple and focused on real client needs, not over-engineering. Robert's expertise will be invaluable.

Next sync with Robert scheduled for Thursday to review architecture approach.

---

**Related Projects**:
- [[OPT - DOME USA]] (parent initiative)
- [[Obsidian Infrastructure]] (similar infrastructure work)

**Tags**: #llm #research #infrastructure #client-work #dome
```

---

## Success Criteria

- ✅ Project note created with complete structure
- ✅ All stakeholders identified and linked
- ✅ Project added to relevant MOC
- ✅ Recurring tasks and milestones defined
- ✅ Success criteria clearly articulated
- ✅ Resources gathered and linked
- ✅ First log entry added
- ✅ People notes updated bidirectionally
- ✅ People - Active Projects list updated

---

## Tips & Best Practices

1. **Use PT/OPT prefix** - Clarifies project type at a glance
2. **3-5 goals max** - More creates diffusion of focus
3. **SMART success criteria** - Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
4. **Link generously** - Every person, related project, resource
5. **Start log immediately** - Establishes pattern, captures context
6. **Realistic timelines** - Pad estimates, things take longer than you think
7. **Clear ownership** - Who's responsible for what
8. **Weekly updates** - Make recurring task for consistent updates

---

## Common Variations

### Quick Project Start (5 min)
- Basic project note (title, goals, people)
- Link to 1 key person
- Add to MOC
- First next action only
- Use for small or exploratory projects

### Comprehensive Project Kickoff (30 min)
- Full template with all sections
- Stakeholder mapping
- Detailed milestone planning
- Resource research
- Risk assessment
- Use for major PT projects or client work

### Team Project Kickoff (45 min)
- Include kickoff meeting notes
- Team roles and responsibilities
- Communication plan
- Decision-making framework
- Use for multi-person projects

---

## Integration Points

**Feeds into**:
- Daily morning routine (next actions surface)
- Evening routine (project updates)
- Weekly planning (ON priority review)
- Monthly review (milestone tracking)

**Depends on**:
- Person notes (stakeholder context)
- MOCs (organizational structure)
- Templates (consistent formatting)

---

## Project Types & Templates

### PT (Primary Thing) - High Focus
- Lives in `3 Efforts/ON/`
- 30-40% time allocation
- Strategic importance
- Your main focus area
- Example: Core product development, major client deliverable

### OPT (Other Priority Thing) - Active Work
- Lives in `3 Efforts/ON/` or `3 Efforts/3 Projects/`
- 20-30% time allocation
- Important but not primary
- Example: Supporting projects, secondary clients

### Ongoing - Continuous Work
- Lives in `3 Efforts/Ongoing/`
- 10-15% time allocation
- Maintenance, operations
- Example: Client support, system maintenance

### Simmering - On Hold
- Lives in `3 Efforts/Simmering/`
- Intentionally paused
- Seasonal or blocked
- Example: Waiting for external input, future opportunity

---

## Checklist

```markdown
### Project Kickoff Checklist

#### Setup
- [ ] Create project note in appropriate location (ON/3 Projects/Ongoing)
- [ ] Use PT/OPT prefix
- [ ] Initialize with template structure
- [ ] Set YAML frontmatter (tags, status, dates)

#### People
- [ ] Identify all stakeholders (owner, collaborators, clients)
- [ ] Link people in project note
- [ ] Update each person's note with this project
- [ ] Update People - Active Projects list
- [ ] Consider relationship tiers

#### Organization
- [ ] Add to relevant MOC (Business/Tech/Personal)
- [ ] Link MOC in project note
- [ ] Link to related projects if applicable
- [ ] Create supporting notes if needed

#### Planning
- [ ] Define 3-5 clear goals
- [ ] Set measurable success criteria
- [ ] Create milestone timeline
- [ ] Identify key deliverables
- [ ] Set up recurring tasks (updates, syncs, reviews)

#### Resources
- [ ] Gather relevant documentation
- [ ] Link to background research
- [ ] List tools and templates
- [ ] Add external references

#### Launch
- [ ] Write first log entry (kickoff context)
- [ ] Define immediate next actions (2-5)
- [ ] Identify any blockers
- [ ] Schedule first stakeholder sync if needed
- [ ] Add to weekly review prompt
```

---

## Red Flags

Watch for these during kickoff (address immediately):

- **Unclear goals** → Can't define success? Need more clarity before starting
- **Too many stakeholders** → > 5 people often indicates scope too large
- **No timeline** → Open-ended projects rarely complete
- **Missing owner** → Who's accountable? Must be clear
- **No success criteria** → How will you know when done?
- **Duplicate effort** → Check for similar existing projects first

---

## After Kickoff

**Immediate next steps**:
1. Schedule first working session (time block)
2. Reach out to key collaborators (initiate)
3. Add to today's daily note (visibility)
4. Set weekly update reminder (Friday)
5. Add to weekly review checklist (track progress)

**Within first week**:
- First substantial progress update in log
- First sync with primary collaborator
- First research/documentation gathered
- First milestone progress (even if small)

---

## Automation Opportunities

**Future enhancements**:
- [ ] Project template with pre-filled structure
- [ ] Auto-link to people based on tags
- [ ] Suggest relevant MOCs based on project type
- [ ] Generate milestone templates by project category
- [ ] Auto-create recurring task reminders
- [ ] Link similar past projects (learning)

---

# Meeting Flow Workflow

**Purpose**: Prepare for, conduct, and follow up on meetings with complete context and action capture

**Triggers**: "meeting with [person]", "prepare for meeting", "meeting prep"

**Duration**:
- Pre-meeting: ~5-10 minutes
- Meeting: Variable
- Post-meeting: ~5-10 minutes

**When to use**: Any scheduled meeting with stakeholders, clients, collaborators, or team members

---

## Workflow Steps

### Phase 1: Pre-Meeting Preparation

#### 1. Pull Person Context
**Skill**: `obsidian-persons`

**Actions**:
- Open person note: `Atlas Dots/Party/[Person Name].md` or `Atlas Dots/[Person Name].md`
- Review:
  - **Relationship tier** (1-5) - informs engagement approach
  - **Recent interactions** - what was last discussed?
  - **Projects in common** - shared context
  - **Waiting-for items** - anything you're expecting from them?
  - **Personal notes** - context clues (family, interests, current situation)
- Note any gaps in relationship (last contact > expected frequency?)

**Output**: Full context on person and relationship

---

#### 2. Find Related Project Notes
**Skills**: Project links from person note, search

**Actions**:
- Identify shared projects from person note
- Open relevant project notes:
  - Current status
  - Recent updates
  - Open questions/blockers
  - Upcoming milestones
- Note discussion points that need addressing
- Identify decisions needed

**Output**: Project context and agenda items

---

#### 3. Create Meeting Note
**Skill**: `obsidian-meeting-notes`

**Actions**:
- Create meeting note: `3 Efforts Notes/Meeting - [Date] - [Person/Topic].md`
- Initialize with standard template:
  - **YAML frontmatter** (date, attendees, tags)
  - **Objective** - why this meeting?
  - **Agenda** - what to cover
  - **Pre-meeting context** - key background
  - **Discussion notes** - space for during meeting
  - **Decisions** - outcomes
  - **Action items** - who does what by when
  - **Follow-ups** - next steps
- Link to:
  - Person note: `[[Person Name]]`
  - Related projects: `[[Project Name]]`
  - Previous meeting notes (if series)

**Output**: Meeting note ready for use during meeting

---

#### 4. Set Meeting Intention
**Skills**: Strategic thinking

**Actions**:
- Clarify meeting purpose:
  - **Information sharing** (status update, context exchange)
  - **Problem solving** (work through challenge together)
  - **Decision making** (resolve open question, commit to direction)
  - **Relationship building** (strengthen connection, explore collaboration)
  - **Planning** (align on timeline, coordinate work)
- Set 1-3 desired outcomes (what success looks like)
- Note any constraints (time limits, decision authority)

**Output**: Clear meeting intention and success criteria

---

### Phase 2: During Meeting

#### 5. Capture Discussion Notes
**Skills**: Active listening, note-taking

**Actions**:
- Use meeting note Discussion section
- Capture key points:
  - Main topics discussed
  - Important context or background shared
  - Concerns or challenges raised
  - Ideas or suggestions
  - Questions asked/answered
- Don't try to transcribe everything - focus on key points
- Note speaker for important quotes or positions

**Output**: Core discussion captured

---

#### 6. Record Decisions
**Skills**: Decision documentation

**Actions**:
- Explicitly note decisions made:
  - What was decided?
  - Who made the decision (if group, how consensus reached)?
  - Rationale (why this choice?)
  - Alternatives considered (what was rejected?)
- Mark clearly with "DECISION:" prefix
- Link to relevant project notes where decision impacts work

**Output**: Clear decision record

---

#### 7. Capture Action Items
**Skills**: Task management

**Actions**:
- For every commitment:
  - **What** - specific action
  - **Who** - owner (clear accountability)
  - **When** - deadline or timeframe
  - **Why** - context (optional but helpful)
- Format: `- [ ] [Action] - @[Owner] - by [Date]`
- Distinguish:
  - Your actions (will add to task list)
  - Their actions (add to person note waiting-for)
  - Shared actions (coordinate)

**Output**: All commitments documented

---

### Phase 3: Post-Meeting Processing

#### 8. Update Person Note
**Skill**: `obsidian-persons`

**Actions**:
- Add meeting to person note:
  - Date of interaction
  - Brief summary (1-2 sentences)
  - Link to meeting note
  - Overall sentiment/tone
- Update relationship data:
  - Last contact date
  - Frequency tracking
  - Relationship health indicator
- Add waiting-for items if applicable:
  - What they committed to
  - Expected delivery date
  - Link to meeting note

**Output**: Person note current with today's interaction

---

#### 9. Update Project Notes
**Skill**: `obsidian-update-project`

**Actions**:
- For each project discussed:
  - Add date-stamped update to project log
  - Note key discussion points
  - Record decisions that impact project
  - Update status if changed
  - Add new tasks to project task list
  - Link to meeting note
- Create bidirectional links (meeting ← → project)

**Output**: Project notes current with meeting outcomes

---

#### 10. Process Action Items
**Skills**: Task management, daily note

**Actions**:
- Your action items:
  - Add to appropriate task tracking (daily note, project note, or lists)
  - Set deadlines in calendar if time-specific
  - Add context (link to meeting note)
  - Estimate effort if needed for time blocking
- Their action items:
  - Add to person note under "Waiting For"
  - Set reminder to follow up if no response by deadline
  - Link to meeting note for context

**Output**: All actions in appropriate tracking systems

---

#### 11. Set Follow-Up Reminders
**Skills**: Recurring task management

**Actions**:
- Determine follow-up needs:
  - **Next meeting** - schedule if recurring or continuation needed
  - **Check-in** - when to follow up on their action items
  - **Decision review** - when to revisit decisions made
  - **Relationship touchpoint** - based on tier frequency expectations
- Add reminders to:
  - Calendar (if specific date)
  - Daily note template (if regular check-in)
  - Person note (as recurring task)

**Output**: Follow-ups scheduled, won't fall through cracks

---

#### 12. Reflect & Learn
**Skills**: Continuous improvement

**Actions**:
- Quick reflection (1-2 minutes):
  - Did meeting achieve desired outcomes?
  - What went well?
  - What could improve next time?
  - Any relationship insights?
- Add brief note in meeting note or daily review
- Identify patterns over time (monthly review data)

**Output**: Learning captured for improvement

---

## Expected Output Format

### Meeting Note Example
```markdown
---
tags:
  - type/meeting
  - person/robert-pratt
  - project/dome-usa
created: 2025-11-09, 14:00
meeting-date: 2025-11-09
attendees:
  - "[[Natie Rautenbach]]"
  - "[[Robert Pratt]]"
status: completed
---
```

# Meeting Flow Workflow

**Purpose**: Prepare for, conduct, and follow up on meetings with complete context and action capture

**Triggers**: "meeting with [person]", "prepare for meeting", "meeting prep"

**Duration**:
- Pre-meeting: ~5-10 minutes
- Meeting: Variable
- Post-meeting: ~5-10 minutes

**When to use**: Any scheduled meeting with stakeholders, clients, collaborators, or team members

---

## Workflow Steps

### Phase 1: Pre-Meeting Preparation

#### 1. Pull Person Context
**Skill**: `obsidian-persons`

**Actions**:
- Open person note: `Atlas Dots/Party/[Person Name].md` or `Atlas Dots/[Person Name].md`
- Review:
  - **Relationship tier** (1-5) - informs engagement approach
  - **Recent interactions** - what was last discussed?
  - **Projects in common** - shared context
  - **Waiting-for items** - anything you're expecting from them?
  - **Personal notes** - context clues (family, interests, current situation)
- Note any gaps in relationship (last contact > expected frequency?)

**Output**: Full context on person and relationship

---

#### 2. Find Related Project Notes
**Skills**: Project links from person note, search

**Actions**:
- Identify shared projects from person note
- Open relevant project notes:
  - Current status
  - Recent updates
  - Open questions/blockers
  - Upcoming milestones
- Note discussion points that need addressing
- Identify decisions needed

**Output**: Project context and agenda items

---

#### 3. Create Meeting Note
**Skill**: `obsidian-meeting-notes`

**Actions**:
- Create meeting note: `3 Efforts Notes/Meeting - [Date] - [Person/Topic].md`
- Initialize with standard template:
  - **YAML frontmatter** (date, attendees, tags)
  - **Objective** - why this meeting?
  - **Agenda** - what to cover
  - **Pre-meeting context** - key background
  - **Discussion notes** - space for during meeting
  - **Decisions** - outcomes
  - **Action items** - who does what by when
  - **Follow-ups** - next steps
- Link to:
  - Person note: `[[Person Name]]`
  - Related projects: `[[Project Name]]`
  - Previous meeting notes (if series)

**Output**: Meeting note ready for use during meeting

---

#### 4. Set Meeting Intention
**Skills**: Strategic thinking

**Actions**:
- Clarify meeting purpose:
  - **Information sharing** (status update, context exchange)
  - **Problem solving** (work through challenge together)
  - **Decision making** (resolve open question, commit to direction)
  - **Relationship building** (strengthen connection, explore collaboration)
  - **Planning** (align on timeline, coordinate work)
- Set 1-3 desired outcomes (what success looks like)
- Note any constraints (time limits, decision authority)

**Output**: Clear meeting intention and success criteria

---

### Phase 2: During Meeting

#### 5. Capture Discussion Notes
**Skills**: Active listening, note-taking

**Actions**:
- Use meeting note Discussion section
- Capture key points:
  - Main topics discussed
  - Important context or background shared
  - Concerns or challenges raised
  - Ideas or suggestions
  - Questions asked/answered
- Don't try to transcribe everything - focus on key points
- Note speaker for important quotes or positions

**Output**: Core discussion captured

---

#### 6. Record Decisions
**Skills**: Decision documentation

**Actions**:
- Explicitly note decisions made:
  - What was decided?
  - Who made the decision (if group, how consensus reached)?
  - Rationale (why this choice?)
  - Alternatives considered (what was rejected?)
- Mark clearly with "DECISION:" prefix
- Link to relevant project notes where decision impacts work

**Output**: Clear decision record

---

#### 7. Capture Action Items
**Skills**: Task management

**Actions**:
- For every commitment:
  - **What** - specific action
  - **Who** - owner (clear accountability)
  - **When** - deadline or timeframe
  - **Why** - context (optional but helpful)
- Format: `- [ ] [Action] - @[Owner] - by [Date]`
- Distinguish:
  - Your actions (will add to task list)
  - Their actions (add to person note waiting-for)
  - Shared actions (coordinate)

**Output**: All commitments documented

---

### Phase 3: Post-Meeting Processing

#### 8. Update Person Note
**Skill**: `obsidian-persons`

**Actions**:
- Add meeting to person note:
  - Date of interaction
  - Brief summary (1-2 sentences)
  - Link to meeting note
  - Overall sentiment/tone
- Update relationship data:
  - Last contact date
  - Frequency tracking
  - Relationship health indicator
- Add waiting-for items if applicable:
  - What they committed to
  - Expected delivery date
  - Link to meeting note

**Output**: Person note current with today's interaction

---

#### 9. Update Project Notes
**Skill**: `obsidian-update-project`

**Actions**:
- For each project discussed:
  - Add date-stamped update to project log
  - Note key discussion points
  - Record decisions that impact project
  - Update status if changed
  - Add new tasks to project task list
  - Link to meeting note
- Create bidirectional links (meeting ← → project)

**Output**: Project notes current with meeting outcomes

---

#### 10. Process Action Items
**Skills**: Task management, daily note

**Actions**:
- Your action items:
  - Add to appropriate task tracking (daily note, project note, or lists)
  - Set deadlines in calendar if time-specific
  - Add context (link to meeting note)
  - Estimate effort if needed for time blocking
- Their action items:
  - Add to person note under "Waiting For"
  - Set reminder to follow up if no response by deadline
  - Link to meeting note for context

**Output**: All actions in appropriate tracking systems

---

#### 11. Set Follow-Up Reminders
**Skills**: Recurring task management

**Actions**:
- Determine follow-up needs:
  - **Next meeting** - schedule if recurring or continuation needed
  - **Check-in** - when to follow up on their action items
  - **Decision review** - when to revisit decisions made
  - **Relationship touchpoint** - based on tier frequency expectations
- Add reminders to:
  - Calendar (if specific date)
  - Daily note template (if regular check-in)
  - Person note (as recurring task)

**Output**: Follow-ups scheduled, won't fall through cracks

---

#### 12. Reflect & Learn
**Skills**: Continuous improvement

**Actions**:
- Quick reflection (1-2 minutes):
  - Did meeting achieve desired outcomes?
  - What went well?
  - What could improve next time?
  - Any relationship insights?
- Add brief note in meeting note or daily review
- Identify patterns over time (monthly review data)

**Output**: Learning captured for improvement

# CLAUDE.md

> Think carefully and implement the most concise solution that changes as little code as possible.

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Django 5.2.4 recruitment platform with AI-powered candidate-employer matching, integrating O*NET occupational data. The system uses PostgreSQL, Redis caching, and Mailjet email integration.

## USE SUB-AGENTS FOR CONTEXT OPTIMIZATION

### 1. Always use the file-analyzer sub-agent when asked to read files

The file-analyzer agent is an expert in extracting and summarizing critical information from files, particularly log files and verbose outputs. It provides concise, actionable summaries that preserve essential information while dramatically reducing context usage.

### 2. Always use the code-analyzer sub-agent when asked to search code, analyze code, research bugs, or trace logic flow

The code-analyzer agent is an expert in code analysis, logic tracing, and vulnerability detection. It provides concise, actionable summaries that preserve essential information while dramatically reducing context usage.

### 3. Always use the test-runner sub-agent to run tests and analyze the test results

Using the test-runner agent ensures:

- Full test output is captured for debugging
- Main conversation stays clean and focused
- Context usage is optimized
- All issues are properly surfaced
- No approval dialogs interrupt the workflow

## Key Commands

### Development

```bash
# Development server
make run                                      # Run on port 8000
python manage.py runserver 8001              # Alternative port

# Database
make migrate                                  # Apply migrations
make makemigrations                          # Create migrations
python manage.py dbshell                     # PostgreSQL access
python manage.py shell                       # Django shell

# Static files & dependencies
make collectstatic                           # Collect static files
make install                                 # Install requirements
```

### Testing

```bash
# Run all tests
python manage.py test                        # All tests
make test                                    # Via Makefile

# App-specific tests
python manage.py test candidates.tests       # Candidate tests
python manage.py test employers.tests        # Employer tests
python manage.py test jobs.tests            # Jobs tests
python manage.py test applications.tests     # Applications tests
python manage.py test occupations.tests     # Occupations tests
python manage.py test shared.tests          # Shared services tests

# Single test file or class
python manage.py test candidates.tests.test_auth
python manage.py test candidates.tests.test_auth.TestOTPThrottling

# Integration tests (standalone scripts)
python jobs/tests/integration/test_improved_search.py
python jobs/tests/integration/test_enhanced_search.py

# Test scripts
python scripts/test_email.py                # Email functionality
python scripts/test_job_application_eligibility.py
```

### Code Quality

**ALWAYS run diagnostics before completing any task:**

- Execute `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` to check all files for linting/type errors
- Fix all issues before considering work complete

### O*NET Data Management

```bash
python manage.py import_onet data/onet/db_30_0_text/          # Import O*NET data
python manage.py import_onet data/onet/db_30_0_text/ --clear  # Clear and reimport
```

## Architecture

### Django Apps Structure

1. **candidates/** - Passwordless auth, CV processing, skill extraction
2. **employers/** - Company management, recruiter auth, dashboard
3. **jobs/** - AI-powered job creation, O*NET matching
4. **applications/** - Application workflow and tracking
5. **occupations/** - 30+ O*NET models and data management
6. **ai_integration/** - OpenRouter/OpenAI provider abstraction
7. **shared/** - Email services, UI components, common utilities

### Service Layer Pattern (Django Styleguide)

Business logic organization:

- **services/** - Write operations, complex business logic
- **selectors/** - Read operations, data fetching
- **serializers.py** - Data validation and formatting
- **views.py** - API endpoints only, no business logic

### Email System Architecture

Multi-provider email system with factory pattern:

- **Providers**: Mailjet (primary), SMTP, Console (dev)
- **Factory**: `shared/services/email_factory.py`
- **Templates**: `templates/emails/` with auth/notifications
- **Configuration**: Environment-based provider selection

### AI Integration

Provider-agnostic LLM interface:

- **Providers**: OpenRouter (primary), OpenAI fallback
- **Service**: `ai_integration/services/chat_service.py`
- **Token tracking**: Automatic logging and rate limiting
- **Configuration**: `LLM_PROVIDER`, API keys in settings

### Testing Organization

```
app_name/
  tests/
    test_models.py
    test_services.py
    test_selectors.py
    test_views.py
    integration/
      test_feature.py
    factories.py
```

## Critical Implementation Details

### Occupation Search Algorithm

`jobs/services/occupation_search.py`:

- Seniority detection maps to Job Zones 1-5
- Domain-aware matching (data, software, finance, medical, marketing)
- Confidence scoring: Exact (95%) → Alternate (90%) → Partial (70-85%) → Word (50-65%)
- AI fallback when < 3 fuzzy matches

### Authentication Flow

**Candidates**: Passwordless with OTP

- 6-digit OTP, 5-minute expiry
- Throttling: 3 attempts per 5 minutes
- Email via Mailjet transactional

**Employers**: Traditional email/password

- Registration with company creation
- Role-based access (admin/recruiter)

### Caching Strategy

Redis caching for dashboard performance:

- Employer dashboard: 5-minute cache
- Candidate recommendations: 15-minute cache
- O*NET data: 1-hour cache

## Environment Variables

```env
# Core Django
SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key
DEBUG=True
DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/recruit_db

# Email (Mailjet)
EMAIL_PROVIDER=mailjet
MAILJET_API_KEY=your-api-key
MAILJET_API_SECRET=your-secret
MAILJET_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@example.com

# AI Integration
LLM_PROVIDER=openrouter
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-xxx
OPENROUTER_MODEL=openai/gpt-4-turbo

# Redis Cache
REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/1

# Feature Flags
ENABLE_AI_MATCHING=True
ENABLE_CV_PROCESSING=True
```

## Development Philosophy

### Tone and Behavior

- Criticism is welcome. Please tell me when I am wrong or mistaken, or even when you think I might be wrong or mistaken.
- Please tell me if there is a better approach than the one I am taking.
- Please tell me if there is a relevant standard or convention that I appear to be unaware of.
- Be skeptical.
- Be concise.
- Short summaries are OK, but don't give an extended breakdown unless we are working through the details of a plan.
- Do not flatter, and do not give compliments unless I am specifically asking for your judgement.
- Occasional pleasantries are fine.
- Feel free to ask many questions. If you are in doubt of my intent, don't guess. Ask.

### ABSOLUTE RULES

- **NO PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION** - Complete features only
- **NO SIMPLIFICATION** - No "//This is simplified stuff for now, complete implementation would blablabla"
- **NO CODE DUPLICATION** - Check existing codebase to reuse functions and constants. Read files before writing new functions. Use common sense function name to find them easily.
- **NO DEAD CODE** - Either use or delete from codebase completely
- **IMPLEMENT TEST FOR EVERY FUNCTIONS** - Every function needs tests
- **NO CHEATER TESTS** - Test must be accurate, reflect real usage and be designed to reveal flaws. No useless tests! Design tests to be verbose so we can use them for debugging.
- **NO INCONSISTENT NAMING** - Read existing codebase naming patterns
- **NO OVER-ENGINEERING** - Don't add unnecessary abstractions, factory patterns, or middleware when simple functions would work. Don't think "enterprise" when you need "working"
- **NO MIXED CONCERNS** - Don't put validation logic inside API handlers, database queries inside UI components, etc. instead of proper separation
- **NO RESOURCE LEAKS** - Don't forget to close database connections, clear timeouts, remove event listeners, or clean up file handles
- **FOLLOW PATTERNS** - Check existing code for conventions:
  - docs/django_styleguide.md
  - SOLID principles
  - TDD Development

### Error Handling

- **Fail fast** for critical configuration (missing text model)
- **Log and continue** for optional features (extraction model)
- **Graceful degradation** when external services unavailable
- **User-friendly messages** through resilience layer

### Testing Requirements

- Always use the test-runner agent to execute tests
- Do not use mock services for anything ever
- Do not move on to the next test until the current test is complete
- If the test fails, consider checking if the test is structured correctly before deciding we need to refactor the codebase
- Tests must be verbose for debugging
- Complete one test before moving to next
- Check test structure before refactoring code

## Current Development Focus

**Active Branch**: `feature/email-mailjet-integration`

- Implementing Mailjet as primary email provider
- Factory pattern for provider selection
- Template-based transactional emails
- OTP throttling and security improvements

- **Multi-tenant Architecture**: Company-based data isolation
- **Caching Strategy**: Multi-tier caching with intelligent invalidation

- **API Security**: Rate limiting, input validation, and comprehensive audit logging

# Mailjet Email Integration Plan ## Executive Summary This document outlines the integration of Mailjet as the primary email service provider for the recruitment platform, focusing on authentication processes (OTP and password reset). The implementation follows Django Styleguide patterns, SOLID principles, and the development philosophy outlined in `docs/development_elon.md`. ## Table of Contents 1. [Current State Analysis](#current-state-analysis) 2. [Requirements & Objectives](#requirements--objectives) 3. [Architecture Design](#architecture-design) 4. [Implementation Plan](#implementation-plan) 5. [Testing Strategy](#testing-strategy) 6. [Deployment & Configuration](#deployment--configuration) 7. [Monitoring & Maintenance](#monitoring--maintenance) ## Current State Analysis ### Existing Email Infrastructure - **Generic Email Service**: `shared/services/email_service.py` - Supports text, HTML, and template-based emails - Uses Django's default SMTP backend - Includes validation and error handling - **OTP Implementation**: `candidates/utils/auth.py` - Console fallback for development - Basic email sending via `send_mail` - 6-digit OTP with 5-minute expiry - **Current Pain Points**: - No dedicated transactional email provider - Limited email tracking and analytics - No template management system - Fallback to console logging in development ### Email Use Cases 1. **Authentication** - OTP for passwordless login - Password reset tokens - Account verification 2. **Future Use Cases** - Application status updates - Job match notifications - Team invitations - System notifications ## Requirements & Objectives ### Functional Requirements - Send OTP codes reliably within 2 seconds - Support HTML and text email formats - Handle rate limiting and throttling - Provide delivery status tracking - Support email templates with variables ### Non-Functional Requirements - 99.9% email delivery rate - < 3 second API response time - Graceful degradation on service failure - Comprehensive logging and monitoring - GDPR-compliant data handling ### Success Criteria - Zero OTP email failures in production - Reduced email sending latency by 50% - Centralized email management - Improved developer experience ## Architecture Design ### Provider Pattern Architecture ``` ┌─────────────────┐ │ Email Service │ (Facade) └────────┬────────┘ │ ┌────────▼────────┐ │Provider Manager │ (Strategy Pattern) └────────┬────────┘ │ ┌────┴────┬─────────┬──────────┐ │ │ │ │ ┌───▼──┐ ┌───▼──┐ ┌────▼───┐ ┌───▼───┐ │Mailjet│ │ SMTP │ │Console │ │Future │ └───────┘ └──────┘ └────────┘ └───────┘ ``` ### Class Structure ```python # shared/services/email_providers/base.py class EmailProvider(ABC): @abstractmethod def send_email(self, **kwargs) -> EmailResult @abstractmethod def send_bulk(self, emails: List) -> BulkResult @abstractmethod def get_status(self, message_id: str) -> Status # shared/services/email_providers/mailjet_provider.py class MailjetProvider(EmailProvider): def __init__(self, api_key, secret_key) def send_email(self, **kwargs) def send_bulk(self, emails) def get_status(self, message_id) def _handle_rate_limit(self) def _format_mailjet_payload(self) ``` ### File Structure ``` shared/ ├── services/ │ ├── email_providers/ │ │ ├── __init__.py │ │ ├── base.py # Abstract provider interface │ │ ├── mailjet_provider.py # Mailjet implementation │ │ ├── smtp_provider.py # SMTP fallback │ │ └── console_provider.py # Development console │ ├── email_service.py # Main service (updated) │ └── email_factory.py # Provider factory ├── tests/ │ └── services/ │ └── email_providers/ │ ├── test_mailjet_provider.py │ ├── test_email_factory.py │ └── test_email_service_integration.py templates/ └── emails/ ├── auth/ │ ├── otp.html │ ├── otp.txt │ ├── password_reset.html │ └── password_reset.txt └── base_email.html ``` ## Implementation Plan ### Phase 1: Infrastructure Setup (Day 1-2) #### Task 1.1: Install Dependencies ```bash pip install mailjet-rest==1.3.4 ``` #### Task 1.2: Create Provider Interface - Create `shared/services/email_providers/base.py` - Define abstract `EmailProvider` class - Define `EmailResult` and `EmailStatus` dataclasses #### Task 1.3: Implement Mailjet Provider - Create `shared/services/email_providers/mailjet_provider.py` - Implement all abstract methods - Add retry logic with exponential backoff - Include rate limiting handling #### Task 1.4: Update Email Service - Refactor `shared/services/email_service.py` - Add provider selection logic - Maintain backward compatibility ### Phase 2: Authentication Integration (Day 3-4) #### Task 2.1: Create Email Templates ```html

Your Login Code

Hello {{ first_name|default:"there" }},

Your one-time login code is:

{{ otp_code }}

This code expires in {{ expiry_minutes }} minutes.

If you didn't request this code, please ignore this email.

© {{ current_year }} {{ company_name }}. All rights reserved.

# AI Integration Service Documentation

## Overview

The AI Integration Service provides a **provider-agnostic interface** for Large Language Model (LLM) interactions within the Django recruitment platform. It abstracts away vendor-specific implementations while providing automatic token logging, error handling, and retry mechanisms.

## Key Features

- 🔄 **Provider Agnostic**: Switch between OpenRouter, Gemini, or other providers via configuration
- 📊 **Token Logging**: Automatic tracking of prompt/completion tokens with timestamps
- 🛡️ **Error Handling**: Exponential backoff retries for rate limits and API errors
- ⚙️ **Settings Driven**: No code changes needed to switch providers
- 🧪 **Test Driven**: 43+ comprehensive tests ensuring reliability
- 🏗️ **SOLID Principles**: Clean architecture following Django Styleguide patterns

## Quick Start

### 1. Basic Usage

```python
from ai_integration import chat_llm

# One-line LLM interaction
response = chat_llm([
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}
])
print(response)  # "Paris"
```

### 2. With Provider Override

```python
# Use specific provider for this request
response = chat_llm(
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
    provider="openrouter",
    model="google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite"
)
```

### 3. Multi-turn Conversation

```python
conversation = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is machine learning?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Machine learning is..."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Can you give me an example?"}
]

response = chat_llm(conversation)
```

## API Reference

### Core Functions

#### `chat_llm(messages, provider=None, model=None, **kwargs)`

Main facade function for LLM chat completions.

**Parameters:**
- `messages` (list): List of message dictionaries with 'role' and 'content'
- `provider` (str, optional): Provider override (defaults to `settings.LLM_PROVIDER`)
- `model` (str, optional): Model override (defaults to provider's default)
- `**kwargs`: Additional provider-specific options

**Returns:**
- `str`: Response content

**Raises:**
- `LLMServiceError`: If the request fails after all retries

**Example:**
```python
response = chat_llm([
    {"role": "user", "content": "Translate 'hello' to French"}
])
```

#### `get_provider(name=None, api_key=None, model=None, **kwargs)`

Factory function to create provider instances.

**Parameters:**
- `name` (str, optional): Provider name (defaults to settings)
- `api_key` (str, optional): API key override
- `model` (str, optional): Model override
- `**kwargs`: Additional provider arguments

**Returns:**
- `BaseLLMProvider`: Configured provider instance

**Example:**
```python
from ai_integration import get_provider

provider = get_provider('openrouter')
response = provider.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])
```

#### `get_available_providers()`

Get information about registered providers.

**Returns:**
- `dict`: Provider information mapping

**Example:**
```python
from ai_integration import get_available_providers

providers = get_available_providers()
# {'openrouter': {'class': 'OpenRouterProvider', 'config': {...}}}
```

```python
# my_app/providers/custom_provider.py

    @property
    def provider_name(self):
        return "custom"
    
    def chat(self, messages, **kwargs):
        # Implement API call logic
        response = self._make_api_call(messages, **kwargs)
        
        return LLMResponse(
            content=response['content'],
            usage=TokenUsage(
                prompt_tokens=response['usage']['prompt_tokens'],
                completion_tokens=response['usage']['completion_tokens'],
                total_tokens=response['usage']['total_tokens']
            ),
            model=self.model,
            provider=self.provider_name
        )
    
    def count_tokens(self, text):
        # Implement token counting logic
        return len(text) // 4
    
    def _make_api_call(self, messages, **kwargs):
        # Custom API implementation
        pass
```

### SOLID Principles Implementation

1. **Single Responsibility**:
   - `TokenRecorder`: Only handles token persistence
   - `ChatService`: Only handles chat orchestration
   - Each provider: Only handles one API integration

2. **Open/Closed**: 
   - New providers can be added without modifying existing code
   - Factory pattern allows extension without modification

3. **Liskov Substitution**:
   - All providers implement `BaseLLMProvider` interface
   - Any provider can be substituted for another

4. **Interface Segregation**:
   - `BaseLLMProvider` defines minimal required interface
   - `TokenRecorder` has focused interface for logging

5. **Dependency Inversion**:
   - Services depend on abstractions (interfaces)
   - Concrete implementations injected via factory

### Error Hierarchy

```
LLMServiceError (base)
├── LLMProviderError
│   ├── LLMProviderNotFoundError
│   ├── LLMProviderConfigurationError
│   ├── LLMProviderRateLimitError
│   ├── LLMProviderAuthenticationError
│   └── LLMProviderAPIError
└── LLMTokenRecorderError
```

```python
from django.core.cache import cache
import hashlib

def cached_llm_call(messages, cache_timeout=3600):
    # Create cache key from messages
    key = hashlib.md5(str(messages).encode()).hexdigest()
    
    # Try cache first
    cached_response = cache.get(f"llm:{key}")
    if cached_response:
        return cached_response
    
    # Make LLM call
    response = chat_llm(messages)
    
    # Cache the response
    cache.set(f"llm:{key}", response, cache_timeout)
    return response
```

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

#### 1. API Key Not Found

```
LLMProviderConfigurationError: API key not found for openrouter. Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY in settings or environment variables.
```

**Solution:** Set the appropriate API key in settings or environment:
```bash
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="your-key-here"
```

#### 2. Provider Not Found

```
LLMProviderNotFoundError: Provider 'custom' not found. Available providers: ['openrouter']
```

**Solution:** Ensure the provider is registered in your app's `ready()` method.

#### 3. Token Log Permission Error

```
LLMTokenRecorderFileError: No write permission for log file: /path/to/llm_tokens.log
```

```python
LLM_TOKEN_LOG_PATH = '/tmp/llm_tokens.log'
```

#### 4. Rate Limiting

```
LLMProviderRateLimitError: Rate limit exceeded
```

**Solution:** The service automatically retries with exponential backoff. If issues persist, check your API quota or implement request queuing.

## Performance Considerations

### Request Batching

For multiple independent requests:

```python
import asyncio
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

async def batch_llm_calls(message_batches):
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as executor:
        loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
        tasks = [
            loop.run_in_executor(executor, chat_llm, messages)
            for messages in message_batches
        ]
        return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
```

```python
from django.core.cache import cache

def rate_limited_llm_call(user_id, messages, limit=10):
    key = f"llm_calls:{user_id}"
    calls = cache.get(key, 0)
    
    if calls >= limit:
        raise Exception("Rate limit exceeded")
    
    cache.set(key, calls + 1, 3600)  # 1 hour window
    return chat_llm(messages)
```

## Monitoring and Observability

### Logging Configuration

The service uses Django's logging framework. Configure in `settings.py`:

```python
LOGGING = {
    'version': 1,
    'disable_existing_loggers': False,
    'handlers': {
        'console': {
            'class': 'logging.StreamHandler',
        },
    },
    'loggers': {
        'ai_integration': {
            'handlers': ['console'],
            'level': 'INFO',
            'propagate': False,
        },
    },
}
```

### Performance Monitoring

The service logs timing information for all requests:

```
INFO LLM request completed - Provider: openrouter, Model: google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite, Duration: 1.23s, Tokens: 45
```

### Error Monitoring

Failed requests are logged with full context:

```
ERROR LLM request failed - Provider: openrouter, Duration: 2.15s, Error: Rate limit exceeded
WARNING LLM request failed (attempt 1/3), retrying in 1.1s: Rate limit exceeded
```

## Implementation Details

### Retry Logic

The service implements exponential backoff with jitter:

```python
# Retry parameters
max_retries = 3
base_delay = 1.0
exponential_base = 2

for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
    try:
        return make_request()
    except RetryableError:
        if attempt < max_retries:
            delay = (exponential_base ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 0.1)
            time.sleep(delay)
```

### Thread Safety

- **Token Recording**: Uses threading.Lock for concurrent writes
- **Provider Factory**: Stateless design allows concurrent usage
- **HTTP Client**: Each provider instance has its own httpx.Client

### Memory Management

- **HTTP Connections**: Automatic connection pooling via httpx
- **Token Logs**: Streaming writes to avoid memory buildup
- **Provider Instances**: Lightweight objects with minimal state

# Knowledge Processing Workflow

**Purpose**: Transform raw information (clippings, notes, ideas) into structured, connected knowledge

**Triggers**: "process knowledge", "process clipping", "add to knowledge base", "organize notes"

**Duration**: ~10-20 minutes per item

**When to use**: Processing web clippings, research notes, ideas, or any raw information that needs integration into vault

---

## Workflow Steps

### 1. Process Clipping into Note
**Skill**: `obsidian-process-clipping`

**Actions**:
- Open raw clipping from `Clippings/` folder
- Review and refine:
  - **Extract key insights** - What's actually valuable?
  - **Summarize in your own words** - Don't just copy/paste
  - **Add context** - Why is this important? How might you use it?
  - **Identify category** - What domain does this belong to?
- Transform into structured note:
  - YAML frontmatter (tags, source, date)
  - Lead paragraph (summary/essence)
  - Main content (organized, cleaned up)
  - Back matter (references, related topics, questions)
- Move from `Clippings/` to appropriate location:
  - Research → `Atlas Dots/Research/[Topic].md`
  - Technical → `Atlas Dots/Tech/[Topic].md`
  - Business → `Atlas Dots/Business/[Topic].md`
  - Personal → appropriate category

**Output**: Structured, valuable note in proper location

---

### 2. Find Connections
**Skill**: `obsidian-find-connections`

**Actions**:
- Analyze new note for connection opportunities:
  - **Similar topics** - What existing notes relate?
  - **People** - Who would care about this?
  - **Projects** - Which active work could use this?
  - **Concepts** - What broader ideas does this connect to?
- Search vault for potential connections:
  - Keyword search (key terms from note)
  - Tag exploration (similar tags)
  - MOC scanning (relevant maps of content)
  - Recent notes review (temporal connections)
- Identify 3-5 most relevant connections

**Output**: List of related notes and concepts

---

### 3. Create Bidirectional Links
**Skill**: `obsidian-interlink`

**Actions**:
- For each connection identified:
  - Add link in new note to existing note
  - Add link in existing note back to new note
  - Add context around link (why is this connected?)
  - Consider link type:
    - **Supports** - provides evidence for
    - **Contradicts** - challenges or disputes
    - **Expands** - adds detail or nuance
    - **Examples** - illustrates concept
    - **Related** - similar topic or theme
- Create meaningful link text (not just `[[Note Title]]`):
  - Use aliases when appropriate
  - Embed context: "As discussed in [[Note]], the key factor..."
  - Link sentences, not just words

**Output**: Rich bidirectional connections established

---

### 4. Add to Relevant MOC
**Skill**: `obsidian-mocs`

**Actions**:
- Identify appropriate Map of Content:
  - Existing MOC → `Atlas Maps/[Category]/[Topic MOC]`
  - Create new MOC if gap exists
- Add note to MOC:
  - Under appropriate section/heading
  - With brief description (1 sentence)
  - In logical order (alphabetical, chronological, or thematic)
- Add MOC link back to note
- Consider MOC hierarchy:
  - Could this note become its own MOC? (if it grows)
  - Should it be in multiple MOCs? (interdisciplinary topics)

**Output**: Note organized in knowledge graph

---

### 5. Link to Projects (if applicable)
**Skills**: Project relevance assessment, `obsidian-update-project`

**Actions**:
- Assess project relevance:
  - Does this inform current work?
  - Does this solve a current problem?
  - Is this reference material for active project?
- If relevant, add to project note:
  - Resources section
  - Link with context (why this is relevant)
  - Update project log if it changes approach
- Consider creating action items:
  - Does this knowledge trigger new tasks?
  - Should this be applied to current work?

**Output**: Knowledge connected to active work

---

### 6. Create Actionable Tasks (if needed)
**Skills**: Task extraction, GTD

**Actions**:
- Review note for actionable insights:
  - Is there something to try/experiment with?
  - A tool/technique to implement?
  - A person to reach out to?

### 1. Process Clipping into Note
**Skill**: `obsidian-process-clipping`

**Actions**:
- Open raw clipping from `Clippings/` folder

  - **Summarize in your own words** - Don't just copy/paste
  - **Add context** - Why is this important? How might you use it?
  - **Identify category** - What domain does this belong to?
- Transform into structured note:
  - YAML frontmatter (tags, source, date)
  - Lead paragraph (summary/essence)
  - Main content (organized, cleaned up)
  - Back matter (references, related topics, questions)
- Move from `Clippings/` to appropriate location:
  - Research → `Atlas Dots/Research/[Topic].md`
  - Technical → `Atlas Dots/Tech/[Topic].md`
  - Business → `Atlas Dots/Business/[Topic].md`
  - Personal → appropriate category

**Output**: Structured, valuable note in proper location

---

### 2. Find Connections
**Skill**: `obsidian-find-connections`

**Actions**:
- Analyze new note for connection opportunities:
  - **Similar topics** - What existing notes relate?
  - **People** - Who would care about this?
  - **Projects** - Which active work could use this?
  - **Concepts** - What broader ideas does this connect to?
- Search vault for potential connections:
  - Keyword search (key terms from note)
  - Tag exploration (similar tags)
  - MOC scanning (relevant maps of content)
  - Recent notes review (temporal connections)
- Identify 3-5 most relevant connections

**Output**: List of related notes and concepts

---

### 3. Create Bidirectional Links
**Skill**: `obsidian-interlink`

**Actions**:
- For each connection identified:
  - Add link in new note to existing note
  - Add link in existing note back to new note
  - Add context around link (why is this connected?)
  - Consider link type:
    - **Supports** - provides evidence for
    - **Contradicts** - challenges or disputes
    - **Expands** - adds detail or nuance
    - **Examples** - illustrates concept
    - **Related** - similar topic or theme
- Create meaningful link text (not just `[[Note Title]]`):
  - Use aliases when appropriate
  - Embed context: "As discussed in [[Note]], the key factor..."
  - Link sentences, not just words

**Output**: Rich bidirectional connections established

---

  - Under appropriate section/heading

- Consider MOC hierarchy:
  - Could this note become its own MOC? (if it grows)

**Output**: Note organized in knowledge graph

  - Is this reference material for active project?
- If relevant, add to project note:
  - Resources section
  - Link with context (why this is relevant)
  - Update project log if it changes approach
- Consider creating action items:
  - Does this knowledge trigger new tasks?
  - Should this be applied to current work?

**Output**: Knowledge connected to active work

  - Technical → `Atlas Dots/Tech/[Topic].md`
  - Business → `Atlas Dots/Business/[Topic].md`
  - Personal → appropriate category

**Output**: Structured, valuable note in proper location

---

### 2. Find Connections
**Skill**: `obsidian-find-connections`

**Actions**:
- Analyze new note for connection opportunities:
  - **Similar topics** - What existing notes relate?
  - **People** - Who would care about this?
  - **Projects** - Which active work could use this?
  - **Concepts** - What broader ideas does this connect to?
- Search vault for potential connections:
  - Keyword search (key terms from note)
  - Tag exploration (similar tags)
  - MOC scanning (relevant maps of content)
  - Recent notes review (temporal connections)
- Identify 3-5 most relevant connections

**Output**: List of related notes and concepts

---

### 3. Create Bidirectional Links
**Skill**: `obsidian-interlink`

**Actions**:
- For each connection identified:
  - Add link in new note to existing note
  - Add link in existing note back to new note
  - Add context around link (why is this connected?)
  - Consider link type:
    - **Supports** - provides evidence for
    - **Contradicts** - challenges or disputes
    - **Expands** - adds detail or nuance
    - **Examples** - illustrates concept
    - **Related** - similar topic or theme
- Create meaningful link text (not just `[[Note Title]]`):
  - Use aliases when appropriate
  - Embed context: "As discussed in [[Note]], the key factor..."
  - Link sentences, not just words

**Output**: Rich bidirectional connections established

---

### 4. Add to Relevant MOC
**Skill**: `obsidian-mocs`

**Actions**:
- Identify appropriate Map of Content:
  - Existing MOC → `Atlas Maps/[Category]/[Topic MOC]`
  - Create new MOC if gap exists
- Add note to MOC:
  - Under appropriate section/heading
  - With brief description (1 sentence)
  - In logical order (alphabetical, chronological, or thematic)
- Add MOC link back to note
- Consider MOC hierarchy:
  - Could this note become its own MOC? (if it grows)
  - Should it be in multiple MOCs? (interdisciplinary topics)

**Output**: Note organized in knowledge graph

---

### 5. Link to Projects (if applicable)
**Skills**: Project relevance assessment, `obsidian-update-project`

**Actions**:
- Assess project relevance:
  - Does this inform current work?
  - Does this solve a current problem?
  - Is this reference material for active project?
- If relevant, add to project note:
  - Resources section
  - Link with context (why this is relevant)
  - Update project log if it changes approach
- Consider creating action items:
  - Does this knowledge trigger new tasks?
  - Should this be applied to current work?

**Output**: Knowledge connected to active work

---

### 6. Create Actionable Tasks (if needed)
**Skills**: Task extraction, GTD

**Actions**:
- Review note for actionable insights:
  - Is there something to try/experiment with?
  - A tool/technique to implement?
  - A person to reach out to?
  - A concept to research further?
- If actionable, create tasks:
  - Quick action (< 2 min) → Do now
  - Project task → Add to relevant project note
  - Someday/maybe → Add to `Atlas Dots/LISTS/Someday.md`
  - Scheduled → Add to calendar or future daily note
- Link task to note (context for future)

**Output**: Knowledge converted to action where appropriate

---

### 7. Add Questions & Future Research
**Skills**: Curiosity tracking, question management

**Actions**:
- Capture open questions:
  - What's unclear or incomplete?
  - What would you like to know more about?
  - What are the limitations of this knowledge?
- Add to note's "Questions" section (back matter)
- Consider creating research tasks:
  - Priority questions → Research now
  - Lower priority → Add to research list
  - Ongoing curiosity → Periodic review
- Link to related questions in other notes

**Output**: Intellectual curiosity captured and tracked

---

### 8. Tag & Categorize
**Skills**: Taxonomy, organization

**Actions**:
- Add appropriate tags:
  - Type tag: `type/research`, `type/reference`, `type/insight`
  - Category tag: `category/llm`, `category/business`, etc.
  - Status tag: `status/in-progress`, `status/evergreen`
  - Custom tags as needed
- Use hierarchical tags for specificity:
  - `tech/ai/llm` not just `llm`
  - `business/strategy/pricing` not just `pricing`
- Limit to 5-7 tags (more reduces usefulness)
- Update YAML frontmatter

**Output**: Note properly categorized for discovery

---

## Expected Output Format

### Processed Knowledge Note Example

```markdown
# RAG Implementation Patterns

**Lead**: Comprehensive overview of Retrieval-Augmented Generation implementation patterns, from naive approaches to advanced techniques. Key insight: Start simple, add complexity only when needed based on evaluation metrics.

---

## Summary

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) enhances LLM outputs by grounding responses in retrieved context. Three main pattern families: Naive RAG, Advanced RAG, and Modular RAG. Each has tradeoffs between complexity and performance.

## Key Insights

### Naive RAG (Recommended Starting Point)
- Simple pipeline: Query → Retrieve → Generate
- Works for 80% of use cases
- Fast to implement, easy to debug
- As [[Robert Pratt]] noted in [[Meeting: Robert Pratt - LLM Pipeline Architecture]], "naive RAG works 80% of time, start there"

### Advanced RAG Patterns
- Query decomposition: Break complex queries into sub-queries
- Re-ranking: Improve retrieved context relevance
- Iterative retrieval: Multiple retrieval rounds
- Use only when naive RAG metrics show need

### Key Success Factors
1. **Quality retrieval** matters more than generation tricks
2. **Evaluation metrics** critical (RAGAS framework recommended)
3. **Chunk size optimization** impacts both retrieval and generation
4. **Metadata filtering** can dramatically improve precision

## Relevant to Projects

This directly informs [[PT - LLM Research Pipeline]] implementation:
- Validates starting with naive RAG approach
- RAGAS framework aligns with Robert's recommendation
- Chunk size experiments should be part of POC

Added to project resources: [[PT - LLM Research Pipeline#Resources]]

## Connections

### Related Concepts
- [[Vector Databases]] - storage layer for retrieval
- [[LLM Evaluation Frameworks]] - assessing RAG quality
- [[Prompt Engineering]] - optimizing generation step
- [[Atlas Maps/Tech/LLM & AI Systems]] - broader context

### Supporting Evidence
- [[Research: RAG vs Fine-tuning]] - when to use each
- [[Tool: LangChain RAG]] - implementation framework

### Contradicts/Challenges
- [[Opinion: Always Use Latest RAG Patterns]] - this argues for starting simple instead

## Implementation Notes

For [[OPT - DOME USA]] work:
- Start with naive RAG (simple retrieve + generate)
- Use Chroma for retrieval (local, simple)
- Implement RAGAS for evaluation
- Only add complexity (re-ranking, query decomposition) if metrics show need

## Source & References

**Original Source**: [Advanced RAG Patterns](https://example.com/rag-patterns)
**Author**: Jane Smith, AI Researcher
```
