# Description

> [!Note]
> **The Capability Intelligence Engine is a core product built on top of the EVOLVE platform.** It provides intelligent content management, automated training updates, and workforce capability mapping - solving the challenge of keeping training content synchronized with changing regulations, equipment, and operational requirements across multiple sites and roles.

# Capability Intelligence Engine - Refined Module Architecture

## **Core Problem Statement**

Content exists in multiple formats across different locations. When regulations change or new equipment is introduced, documentation in multiple places must be updated. Currently extremely difficult and time-consuming to track manually. AI + RAG + intelligence will tag all content, regulations, and skills so that when new documentation comes in, the system can identify exactly which existing materials need updating.

---

## **Three Major System Categories**

### **CATEGORY 1: Content Ingestion & Processing System**

_Handles bringing content in and making it intelligent_

#### **1. Content Ingestion Engine**

- **Function**: Single entry point for all content types (digitized documents, videos, audio, SCORM packages)
- **Sources**: Existing learning repositories, regulatory documents, site-specific materials, equipment manuals
- **Output**: Structured content ready for AI processing

#### **2. SkillTag AI (Content Classification and Tagging)**

- **Function**: Comprehensive AI tagging of content based on roles, skills, regulations, equipment
- **Key Feature**: Creates the "tag mapping" that shows what each piece of documentation relates to
- **Output**: Fully tagged content with metadata linking to roles, skills, regulations, equipment

#### **3. Legacy Content Processor (Physical/Old Material Processing)**

- **Function**: Handles conversion and processing of older materials, transcripts for video/audio
- **Key Feature**: Brings legacy content into the intelligent tagging system
- **Output**: Legacy materials converted to tagged, searchable format

---

### **CATEGORY 2: Content Intelligence & Update System**

_Handles regulatory changes and equipment updates_

#### **4. RegulationSync AI (Material Review Against Requirements)**

- **Function**: Ingests new regulations and equipment documentation
- **Key Feature**: Identifies which existing tagged content needs updates based on new requirements
- **Output**: Precise list of materials requiring modification due to regulatory/equipment changes

#### **5. Content Update AI (Automated Material Modification)**

- **Function**: Takes RegulationSync AI outputs and assists in updating materials
- **Key Feature**: Uses the tag mapping to automatically suggest or make content changes
- **Output**: Updated materials reflecting new regulations/equipment requirements

#### **6. Content Guardian (Version Control and Change Management)**

- **Function**: Manages content versions, tracks changes, prevents duplication
- **Key Feature**: Maintains audit trail of what changed, when, and why
- **Output**: Single source of truth with complete change history

---

### **CATEGORY 3: Site-Specific Personalization & Delivery System**

_Handles role variations across different sites and contexts_

#### **7. SiteAlign AI (Role Standardization & Site-Specific Mapping)**

- **Function**: Maps standardized roles to site-specific variations and requirements
- **Key Feature**: Understands that "gold underground" ≠ "open pit coal mine" even for same base role
- **Input**: Site data, local regulations, equipment variations, geographical requirements
- **Output**: Site-specific role definitions and training requirements

#### **8. Pathway Builder (Personalized Learning Generation)**

- **Function**: Creates personalized learning journeys based on role, site, and regulatory requirements
- **Key Feature**: Uses SiteAlign outputs to generate contextually appropriate learning paths
- **Output**: Customized curricula for specific roles at specific sites

#### **9. Multi-Language Content Engine**

- **Function**: Generates content in multiple languages based on site requirements
- **Key Feature**: Maintains technical accuracy across languages while preserving regulatory compliance
- **Output**: Localized content maintaining compliance and technical precision

---

## **Supporting Infrastructure Systems**

#### **10. Knowledge Hub (Centralized Content Repository)**

- **Function**: Centralized storage with SharePoint Online integration
- **Key Feature**: Single source of truth with robust search capabilities
- **Integration**: Links to existing LMS systems

#### **11. Certification Tracker**

- **Function**: Tracks learner certifications and training due dates
- **Key Feature**: Proactive notification of certification renewals and required updates
- **Data Source**: Learner completion data from LMS integration
- **Output**: Certification status and renewal schedules

#### **12. SME Connect (Expert Validation Hub)**

- **Function**: Human-in-the-loop validation via Power Apps interface
- **Key Feature**: Subject Matter Experts validate AI-generated tags and content updates
- **Workflow**: Routes content requiring human review to appropriate experts

#### **13. ProcessFlow Orchestrator (Workflow Management)**

- **Function**: Orchestrates the entire content lifecycle from ingestion to delivery
- **Key Feature**: Manages handoffs between AI systems and human validation
- **Integration**: Power Automate for workflow automation

#### **14. Analytics Dashboard (System Intelligence)**

- **Function**: Provides visibility into system performance and content status
- **Key Metrics**: Content coverage, update compliance, certification tracking, multilingual coverage
- **Platform**: Power BI integration

---

## **Key System Capabilities Confirmed**

### **Intelligent Content Mapping**

- Every piece of content tagged with roles, skills, regulations, equipment
- Visual mapping shows relationships between content and requirements
- When new documentation arrives, system identifies all related existing content

### **Site-Specific Intelligence**

- Understands role variations across different:
    - Mining types (underground gold vs open pit coal)
    - Geographic locations and local regulations
    - Equipment variations and site-specific procedures

### **Proactive Update Management**

- New regulation → system identifies all affected content automatically
- New equipment → system maps to existing roles and identifies training gaps
- Reduces manual tracking from "extremely time-consuming" to automated

### **Multi-Language Compliance**

- Technical content maintained accurately across languages
- Regulatory compliance preserved in translations
- Site-specific language requirements supported

### **Certification Intelligence**

- Complete learner profile with certification status
- Proactive identification of training renewal requirements
- Integration with existing LMS for seamless workflow

---

## **Critical Success Factors**

1. **Tag Quality**: The intelligence of the entire system depends on comprehensive, accurate tagging
2. **Site Data Accuracy**: SiteAlign AI requires detailed, current site-specific information
3. **SME Engagement**: Human validation critical for maintaining content quality
4. **LMS Integration**: Seamless flow between intelligence engine and existing learning delivery systems


---

## **Relationship to EVOLVE Platform**

The Capability Intelligence Engine is **built on top of EVOLVE** and represents a specialized application of the EVOLVE platform's core capabilities.

### EVOLVE Foundation (Platform Layer):
- **Core LLM + RAG System** - Ingests and processes company knowledge
- **Specialized SLMs** - Creates department/function-specific AI assistants
- **Self-Learning Loop** - Continuously improves from user interactions
- **Digital Twin Technology** - Virtual replicas of processes and systems
- **Privacy-First Architecture** - Runs within client infrastructure

### Capability Intelligence Engine (Product Layer):
Takes EVOLVE's foundation and applies it specifically to **workforce capability management**:
- Uses EVOLVE's RAG to ingest training content, regulations, equipment manuals
- Uses EVOLVE's SLMs to create specialized agents for content tagging, update detection, pathway building
- Uses EVOLVE's learning loop to improve content mapping and regulatory matching over time
- Uses EVOLVE's digital twins to model role variations across sites
- Maintains EVOLVE's privacy-first approach for sensitive training and compliance data

### TTRO Delivery Layer:
- **Micro-learning mobile app** - Learner-facing delivery platform
- **AI Coach** - Hyper-personalized learning experiences
- **Learn when, where, and how** - Flexible learner-centric approach
- **"Never Stop Learning"** - Continuous development philosophy

**Key Insight:** The Capability Intelligence Engine demonstrates EVOLVE's ability to be configured for specific industry/function challenges. Other specialized applications could include sales intelligence, operations optimization, or compliance management - all built on the same EVOLVE foundation.

---

## **TTRO's Four Strategic Pillars**

The Capability Intelligence Engine is designed around **4 strategic themes** that address global AI challenges in learning and workforce development:

### **1. SOVEREIGNTY** 🔒
**Challenges:** How do we maintain control? Where does data reside? How do we comply with global and local regulatory context?

**Capability Intelligence Engine Response:**
- **'Black box' secure environment** - Sovereign learning environments
- **Small Language Models (SLMs)** - Client-controlled, privacy-first AI
- **Client infrastructure deployment** - Data never leaves organizational control
- **Regulatory context design** - Built to comply with local and global regulations

**EVOLVE Foundation:** Privacy-first architecture enables true data sovereignty - the platform runs entirely within client infrastructure with no external data leakage.

---

### **2. ETHICAL AI** ⚖️
**Challenges:** Fair and inclusive AI, unbiased, transparent, responsible use of AI in decision-making.

**Capability Intelligence Engine Response:**
- **Integrated bias mitigation** - Built-in fairness checks
- **Audit trails** - Complete transparency and traceability
- **Human-in-the-loop** - SME validation and oversight (SME Connect module)
- **Learner empowerment focus** - AI augments humans, doesn't replace them

**EVOLVE Foundation:** Self-learning loop includes human validation cycles, ensuring AI recommendations are reviewed and ethical considerations maintained.

---

### **3. AGENTIC AI** 🤖
**Challenges:** Expectations of productivity, more work with less staff, focus on curated and personalized learning.

**Capability Intelligence Engine Response:**
- **AI agentic by design** - Digital agents handle routine intelligence tasks
- **Digital agents** - Specialized AI assistants for each component (SkillTag AI, RegulationSync AI, etc.)
- **Personalized development journeys** - AI coach delivers hyper-personalized learning
- **Responsive and adaptive** - Continuous assessment identifies skill decay and adaptation needs

**EVOLVE Foundation:** Specialized SLMs create department/function-specific agents that work autonomously within defined parameters while learning from interactions.

---

### **4. SUSTAINABILITY/ESG** 🌱
**Challenges:** Equitable solution/participation, carbon footprint, long-term social impact.

**Capability Intelligence Engine Response:**
- **Computational efficiency** - SLMs reduce emissions vs. large models
- **Ethical data sourcing and use** - Purpose-driven AI implementation
- **Equity and impact focus** - Accessible learning for all workforce levels
- **Long-term capability building** - Sustainable skills development, not one-off training

**EVOLVE Foundation:** Ultra-lean technology stack and SLM approach dramatically reduce computational requirements and carbon footprint compared to traditional LLM-only approaches.

---

**Source:** University of Pretoria FODES Presentation (October 2025)

**Date:** 2025-11-05
**Attendees:** [[Ignatius Rautenbach]], [[Kirsty Chadwick]]
**Duration:** ~29 minutes
**Meeting Type:** Strategic Partnership Update
**Status:** 🟡 Action Items Identified

- [[OPT TTRO Saudi Arabia Education Training 202508]]

---

## 📊 Meeting Summary

### Context
Regular update meeting with Kirsty Chadwick (Group CEO, TTRO). Ignatius acknowledged feeling he hasn't been servicing the relationship well enough or leveraging the network effectively. This meeting focused on aligning on opportunities across Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and UAE markets.

### Key Topics Covered
1. **AI Training Course Development** - New offering for TTRO clients
2. **Mazars/Forvis Mazars Partnership** - Major partnership opportunity
3. **Saudi Arabia Expansion** - Formalizing Connect/Yentra agreement
4. **Anglo American Revival** - New opportunity via HR Technologies
5. **Dubai Expansion** - Airports academy and HNW network

### Strategic Themes
- **Sovereign AI** as primary positioning for Saudi market
- **Capability Intelligence Engine** gaining traction across multiple clients
- **Partnership model** - TTRO handles client relationships, Yentra provides technology
- **Geographic expansion** - Coordinated approach across MENA region

---

## 🎯 Strategic Updates by Category

### 1️⃣ AI Training & Course Content

**What:** Ignatius has developed comprehensive AI training materials through ESG Institute diploma work and Oxford research.

**Content Available:**
- AI implementation frameworks for executives
- Sovereignty and ethics considerations
- Assessment tools and methodologies
- Ready-to-deploy training modules

**TTRO Application:**
Can create AI training courses quickly for TTRO clients on:
- How to use AI in your company
- Executive implementation strategies
- AI governance frameworks
- Risk assessment methodologies

**Status:** ✅ Content ready, can be packaged for TTRO delivery

---

### 2️⃣ Mazars/Forvis Mazars Partnership 🆕

**Overview:**
Forvis Mazars (top 3 audit firm globally) launched an institute 18 months ago. Director (Judy) is looking for solutions to offer their clients.

**Opportunity Scope:**
1. **Leadership Capability Academy** - TTRO's existing offering that Mazars doesn't have
2. **AI Skills Training** - Clients asking how to skill their organization with AI
3. **Revenue Model** - Partnership agreement where:
   - Mazars generates revenue through their massive client base
   - TTRO does delivery and heavy lifting
   - Both parties benefit from complementary strengths

**Key Contacts:**
- **Judy** - Director of Mazars Institute
- **CEO** - Final decision maker (meeting being arranged)

**Next Steps:**
- Kirsty + Judy prep business case
- Document product lines TTRO can bring through institute
- Project revenue expectations
- Present to Mazars CEO with compelling business case

**Strategic Value:**
- Access to Mazars' enormous client base
- Partnership with top-tier global firm
- Multiple product lines (leadership + AI)
- Mazars desperate to grow institute revenue

**Project File:** [[OPT TTRO Mazars Partnership 202511]] 🆕

---

### 3️⃣ Saudi Arabia - Formalizing the Partnership

**Current Status:**
Working relationship exists but needs formal structure before JV between TTRO and Energy Tech completes.

**Strategic Urgency:**
Kirsty wants partnerships cemented NOW while she has autonomy, before JV completion requires additional approvals and slows things down.

**Agreement Structure:**

Three primary focus areas for the Kingdom:
1. **🏛️ National Sovereign AI Initiatives** - Ministry/government level
2. **🎓 Academic Space** - Universities, schools, education sector
3. **🏢 Corporate Enterprise** - Private sector implementations

All framed through **Sovereign AI** lens - positioning as strategic national capability.

**Connect/Yentra Relationship:**
- Formal agreement between TTRO + Connect (gives access to Yentra/EVOLVE)
- Ignatius has full autonomy - no need for Gfinity approvals
- Existing MOU already public about TTRO and Evolve Yentra
- Ring-fenced to Saudi entity specifically

**New Opportunities Identified:**

#### Security Sector Skills Development
- **Context:** Saudi has major events leading to 2030 (World Cup, Vision 2030 realization events)
- **Request:** Minister of Economy/Tourism asked Energy Tech to partner on security sector skills
- **Scope:** Development of skills needed for security around large-scale national events
- **Status:** Energy Tech asked if TTRO can do this - answer: yes

#### Physical Security "Hackathon"
- **Request:** Run a hackathon for safety and security (physical, NOT cyber security)
- **Clarification Needed:** Exact format unclear - is it traditional 24-hour hackathon or security event?
- **Ignatius Assessment:** Probably want security event, not coding hackathon
- **Action Required:** Get clarity on actual requirements

#### Teresa 3D Drone Technology
- **Technology:** Advanced 3D modeling via drone for venue mapping and security
- **Current Use:** FIFA World Cup venues in US
- **Saudi Application:** Perfect for event security and venue management
- **Company:** Teresa's company (Ignatius has relationship)
- **Action Required:**
  1. Schedule demo for Abdulhamid and Basam (Saudi contacts)
  2. Lock down Teresa with proper contract/NDA before introduction
  3. Ensure can't bypass and go direct to Saudi market

**Isle of Man SAICA System:**
Ignatius mentioned practice management software from 2018 SAICA tour:
- Tracks all tasks and time for accounting practices
- Shows who's actually working (transparency can be controversial)
- Risk and audit tracking built-in
- Successful implementation with one large practice
- Could be relevant for TTRO's accounting firm clients

**Project File:** [[OPT TTRO Saudi Arabia Education Training 202508]] ✏️ Updated

---

### 4️⃣ Anglo American - New Opening via HR Technologies

**Previous Status:**
- Stalled in Learning & Development space
- L&D roles crushed at group level
- No traction with existing contacts

**Major Development:**
**Sumit** (primary contact) has been **moved from L&D to HR Technologies** (effective November 1, 2025)

**Why This Changes Everything:**
- Capability Intelligence Engine is fundamentally an **HR problem**, not just L&D
- HR Technologies has higher-level stakeholders
- Can now approach:
  - **Chief Digital Officer (CDO)**
  - **Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO)**

**Ignatius Strategic Insight:**
"This problem is a very wide problem, and it's a generic one that most companies will face. You can take this to a CFO because it is a risk profile. Making sure that your people are up to date, how do you retool and reskill? It almost doesn't matter which one of the execs you approach - it's a problem that they need solving."

**Repositioning Strategy:**
- Frame as HR technology solution (not learning content)
- Emphasize risk management angle (CFO-level concern)
- Focus on workforce capability as strategic asset
- Position as solving C-suite problem, not training department problem

**Next Steps:**
- Wait until after November 1 for Sumit to settle into new role
- Hit him up to reopen conversation in HR Technologies context
- Request introduction to CDO and/or CHRO
- Present Capability Intelligence Engine at strategic level

**Assessment:** 🟢 Not doom and gloom - actually better positioning than L&D

**Project File:** [[PT Anglo 202507 Ai Training]] ✏️ Updated

### 5️⃣ Dubai - Airports Academy & HNW Network 🆕

#### Dubai Airports Academy

**Introduction Status:**
- Kirsty introduced Capability Intelligence Engine to Dubai Airports
- Very positive reception

**Opportunity Scope:**
Building an academy for **cross-mobility** for Dubai city:
- Dubai Government initiative (all transportation under one authority)
- Airports + broader city mobility integration
- Preparation for new airport opening

**Key Contact:**
- **Emirati lady** - Recently took Group Learning role at Dubai Airports
- Smart, young, capable
- Sits on Dubai Government committee
- Well-connected at government level

**Strategic Value:**
- Dubai Government backing
- Cross-mobility scope (beyond just airports)

## GDPR Phase 1 Implementation Plan (30 Tasks, 5 Weeks)

### Week 1: Foundation & Authentication Hardening
**Database Changes:**
- Create migration for User model enhancements (session tracking, last_login)
- Add indexes for performance (email lookups, session queries)

**Code Implementation:**
1. Enforce HTTPS in production settings (SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, session cookies)
2. Verify password hashing (should already use Django's PBKDF2)
3. Add role-based middleware for Candidate/Employer separation
4. Implement session timeout logic (30min idle, configurable)
5. Add foreign key constraints check to prevent orphaned records

**Testing:**
- Unit tests for role-based access
- Integration tests for session timeout
- Security tests for HTTPS enforcement

---

### Week 2: Privacy Policy & Access Controls
**New Django App/Models:**
- Create `privacy` app with models:
  - `PolicyVersion` (version, content, effective_date, is_active)
  - `PolicyAcceptance` (user, policy_version, accepted_at, ip_address)

**Templates & Views:**
- Privacy Policy page (template + view)
- Terms of Service page (template + view)
- Footer links component (reusable across all pages)
- Consent checkbox component for registration forms

**Access Control Implementation:**
- Decorator: `@employer_required` for applicant views
- Decorator: `@admin_required` for sensitive operations
- Update employers/views.py to enforce access controls
- Update applications/views.py to restrict candidate data access

**Testing:**
- Test policy page rendering
- Test access control decorators
- Test consent logging with IP capture

---

### Week 3: Account Deletion & Consent Management
**Database Changes:**
- Add to Candidate model: `account_closed_at`, `deletion_requested_at`
- Add to Employer model: `account_closed_at`, `can_delete` (computed property)
- Create `DeletionLog` model (user_id, email, deleted_by, deleted_at, reason, data_snapshot)

**New Features:**
1. Account deletion API endpoint (`/api/account/delete/`)
2. "Delete My Account" button in user settings
3. Deletion confirmation modal (front-end)
4. Email confirmation after deletion (Mailjet integration)
5. Soft delete first (mark inactive), hard delete after 30 days (cron job)

**Services to Create:**
- `account_deletion_service.py`:
  - `request_account_deletion()` - soft delete, log, email
  - `confirm_account_deletion()` - hard delete with cascade
  - `can_delete_employer()` - check for active jobs/applications
  - `anonymize_user_data()` - PII scrubbing for retention

**Testing:**
- Test deletion API with various user states
- Test employer deletion prevention (active jobs)
- Test deletion email sending
- Test audit log creation

---

### Week 4: Data Retention Rules & Employer Deletion
**New Models:**
- `DataRetentionPolicy` (entity_type, retention_days, description, is_active)
- `FinancialRecord` (separate from User, 7-year retention)

**Business Logic Implementation:**
1. Employer deletion rules:
   - Check for active jobs (prevent deletion)
   - Check for applications in last 18 months (prevent deletion)
   - Allow deletion if all jobs closed >24 months
2. Active account retention check (login activity)
3. Financial records separation from user accounts

**Database Migrations:**
- Create `financial_records` table
- Migrate any existing financial data from user records
- Add retention policy seed data

**Configuration:**
- Add retention settings to Django settings.py:
  ```python
  DATA_RETENTION = {
      'INACTIVE_CANDIDATE_MONTHS': 36,
      'JOB_APPLICATION_MONTHS': 18,
      'JOB_POSTING_MONTHS': 24,
      'USAGE_LOGS_MONTHS': 24,
      'SUPPORT_TICKETS_MONTHS': 12,
      'EMPLOYER_FINANCIAL_YEARS': 7
  }
  ```

**Testing:**
- Test employer deletion business rules
- Test financial record separation
- Test retention policy configuration

---

### Week 5: Automation Scripts & Cron Jobs
**Management Commands to Create:**
1. `manage.py delete_inactive_candidates` (36 months threshold)
2. `manage.py cleanup_job_applications` (18 months post-closure)
3. `manage.py cleanup_job_postings` (24 months post-expiry)
4. `manage.py cleanup_usage_logs` (24 months)
5. `manage.py cleanup_support_tickets` (12 months)
6. `manage.py cleanup_marketing_consent_logs` (retain indefinitely, just log rotation)

**Cron Job Setup:**
- Create `scripts/gdpr_cleanup.sh` wrapper
- Add to crontab (daily 2 AM): `0 2 * * * /path/to/gdpr_cleanup.sh`
- Add logging to `/var/log/gdpr_cleanup.log`
- Add Slack/email notifications for cleanup summary

**Monitoring & Reporting:**
- Create `GDPRComplianceReport` model (date, records_deleted, entity_type, log)
- Dashboard view for admins to see retention activity
- Weekly summary email to admin

**Testing:**
- Test each management command in isolation
- Test edge cases (exactly 36 months, one day before threshold)
- Test dry-run mode for all commands
- Integration test for full cleanup workflow

---

### Supporting Infrastructure (Throughout)

**Audit Logging System:**
- Create `shared/audit_log.py` service:
  - `log_sensitive_action(user, action, entity, metadata)`
  - Log all: deletion requests, policy acceptances, admin access to PII, data exports
- Create `AuditLog` model (timestamp, user, action, entity_type, entity_id, ip_address, metadata_json)

**Analytics Anonymization:**
- Create `analytics_jobs` table (anonymized job matching data)
- Service: `anonymize_for_analytics()` - strip PII before analytics export
- Ensure no candidate names/emails in analytics dataset

**Documentation Updates:**
- Update `PRE_DEPLOYMENT.md` checklist
- Create `docs/gdpr/COMPLIANCE_GUIDE.md`
- Update Privacy Policy with actual data retention periods
- Update architecture docs with new models/services

---

### Implementation Order Summary

**Week 1:** Settings, auth hardening, role enforcement (5 tasks)
**Week 2:** Privacy pages, consent tracking, access controls (6 tasks)  
**Week 3:** Deletion API, soft delete, audit logging (7 tasks)
**Week 4:** Retention rules, employer deletion logic, financial records (6 tasks)
**Week 5:** Cron jobs, management commands, monitoring (6 tasks)

**Total:** 30 tasks across 5 weeks

---

### Files to Create/Modify

**New Apps:**
- `privacy/` (models, views, templates for policy management)

**New Models:**
- `PolicyVersion`, `PolicyAcceptance`, `DeletionLog`, `DataRetentionPolicy`, `FinancialRecord`, `AuditLog`, `GDPRComplianceReport`

**Modified Models:**
- `candidates.Candidate` (add account_closed_at, deletion_requested_at)
- `employers.User` (add account_closed_at, session tracking)

**New Services:**
- `shared/audit_log.py`
- `shared/gdpr_compliance.py` (account deletion, anonymization)
- `shared/data_retention.py` (retention rule enforcement)

**New Management Commands:**
- `delete_inactive_candidates.py`
- `cleanup_job_applications.py`
- `cleanup_job_postings.py`
- `cleanup_usage_logs.py`
- `cleanup_support_tickets.py`

**New Templates:**
- `privacy/privacy_policy.html`
- `privacy/terms_of_service.html`
- `shared/components/consent_checkbox.html`
- `shared/components/footer_policy_links.html`
- `account/delete_confirmation_modal.html`

**Configuration:**
- Update `settings.py` (SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, session settings, retention config)
- Create `scripts/gdpr_cleanup.sh`
- Update `requirements.txt` (no new dependencies needed)

---

### Testing Strategy

**Unit Tests:** ~60 tests (each model, service, management command)
**Integration Tests:** ~20 tests (deletion workflow, retention automation, consent flow)
**E2E Tests:** ~10 tests (user journey for deletion, policy acceptance)

**Total Test Coverage Goal:** 95%+ for GDPR-related code

---

### Deployment Checklist Before Starting

1. ✅ Verify current Django version (5.2.4 confirmed)
2. ✅ Backup production database
3. ✅ Create feature branch: `feature/gdpr-phase-1`
4. ✅ Review Obsidian project files for latest requirements

## GDPR Phase 1 Implementation Plan (30 Tasks, 5 Weeks)

### Week 1: Foundation & Authentication Hardening
**Database Changes:**
- Create migration for User model enhancements (session tracking, last_login)
- Add indexes for performance (email lookups, session queries)

**Code Implementation:**
1. Enforce HTTPS in production settings (SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, session cookies)
2. Verify password hashing (should already use Django's PBKDF2)
3. Add role-based middleware for Candidate/Employer separation
4. Implement session timeout logic (30min idle, configurable)
5. Add foreign key constraints check to prevent orphaned records

**Testing:**
- Unit tests for role-based access
- Integration tests for session timeout
- Security tests for HTTPS enforcement

---

### Week 2: Privacy Policy & Access Controls
**New Django App/Models:**
- Create `privacy` app with models:
  - `PolicyVersion` (version, content, effective_date, is_active)
  - `PolicyAcceptance` (user, policy_version, accepted_at, ip_address)

**Templates & Views:**
- Privacy Policy page (template + view)
- Terms of Service page (template + view)
- Footer links component (reusable across all pages)
- Consent checkbox component for registration forms

**Access Control Implementation:**
- Decorator: `@employer_required` for applicant views
- Decorator: `@admin_required` for sensitive operations
- Update employers/views.py to enforce access controls
- Update applications/views.py to restrict candidate data access

**Testing:**
- Test policy page rendering
- Test access control decorators
- Test consent logging with IP capture

---

### Week 3: Account Deletion & Consent Management
**Database Changes:**
- Add to Candidate model: `account_closed_at`, `deletion_requested_at`
- Add to Employer model: `account_closed_at`, `can_delete` (computed property)
- Create `DeletionLog` model (user_id, email, deleted_by, deleted_at, reason, data_snapshot)

**New Features:**
1. Account deletion API endpoint (`/api/account/delete/`)
2. "Delete My Account" button in user settings
3. Deletion confirmation modal (front-end)
4. Email confirmation after deletion (Mailjet integration)
5. Soft delete first (mark inactive), hard delete after 30 days (cron job)

**Services to Create:**
- `account_deletion_service.py`:
  - `request_account_deletion()` - soft delete, log, email
  - `confirm_account_deletion()` - hard delete with cascade
  - `can_delete_employer()` - check for active jobs/applications
  - `anonymize_user_data()` - PII scrubbing for retention

**Testing:**
- Test deletion API with various user states
- Test employer deletion prevention (active jobs)
- Test deletion email sending
- Test audit log creation

---

### Week 4: Data Retention Rules & Employer Deletion
**New Models:**
- `DataRetentionPolicy` (entity_type, retention_days, description, is_active)
- `FinancialRecord` (separate from User, 7-year retention)

**Business Logic Implementation:**
1. Employer deletion rules:
   - Check for active jobs (prevent deletion)
   - Check for applications in last 18 months (prevent deletion)
   - Allow deletion if all jobs closed >24 months
2. Active account retention check (login activity)
3. Financial records separation from user accounts

**Database Migrations:**
- Create `financial_records` table
- Migrate any existing financial data from user records
- Add retention policy seed data

**Configuration:**
- Add retention settings to Django settings.py:
  ```python
  DATA_RETENTION = {
      'INACTIVE_CANDIDATE_MONTHS': 36,
      'JOB_APPLICATION_MONTHS': 18,
      'JOB_POSTING_MONTHS': 24,
      'USAGE_LOGS_MONTHS': 24,
      'SUPPORT_TICKETS_MONTHS': 12,
      'EMPLOYER_FINANCIAL_YEARS': 7
  }
  ```

**Testing:**
- Test employer deletion business rules
- Test financial record separation
- Test retention policy configuration

---

### Week 5: Automation Scripts & Cron Jobs
**Management Commands to Create:**
1. `manage.py delete_inactive_candidates` (36 months threshold)
2. `manage.py cleanup_job_applications` (18 months post-closure)
3. `manage.py cleanup_job_postings` (24 months post-expiry)
4. `manage.py cleanup_usage_logs` (24 months)
5. `manage.py cleanup_support_tickets` (12 months)
6. `manage.py cleanup_marketing_consent_logs` (retain indefinitely, just log rotation)

**Cron Job Setup:**
- Create `scripts/gdpr_cleanup.sh` wrapper
- Add to crontab (daily 2 AM): `0 2 * * * /path/to/gdpr_cleanup.sh`
- Add logging to `/var/log/gdpr_cleanup.log`
- Add Slack/email notifications for cleanup summary

**Monitoring & Reporting:**
- Create `GDPRComplianceReport` model (date, records_deleted, entity_type, log)
- Dashboard view for admins to see retention activity
- Weekly summary email to admin

**Testing:**
- Test each management command in isolation
- Test edge cases (exactly 36 months, one day before threshold)
- Test dry-run mode for all commands
- Integration test for full cleanup workflow

---

### Supporting Infrastructure (Throughout)

**Audit Logging System:**
- Create `shared/audit_log.py` service:
  - `log_sensitive_action(user, action, entity, metadata)`
  - Log all: deletion requests, policy acceptances, admin access to PII, data exports
- Create `AuditLog` model (timestamp, user, action, entity_type, entity_id, ip_address, metadata_json)

**Analytics Anonymization:**
- Create `analytics_jobs` table (anonymized job matching data)
- Service: `anonymize_for_analytics()` - strip PII before analytics export
- Ensure no candidate names/emails in analytics dataset

**Documentation Updates:**
- Update `PRE_DEPLOYMENT.md` checklist
- Create `docs/gdpr/COMPLIANCE_GUIDE.md`
- Update Privacy Policy with actual data retention periods
- Update architecture docs with new models/services

---

### Implementation Order Summary

**Week 1:** Settings, auth hardening, role enforcement (5 tasks)
**Week 2:** Privacy pages, consent tracking, access controls (6 tasks)  
**Week 3:** Deletion API, soft delete, audit logging (7 tasks)
**Week 4:** Retention rules, employer deletion logic, financial records (6 tasks)
**Week 5:** Cron jobs, management commands, monitoring (6 tasks)

**Total:** 30 tasks across 5 weeks

---

### Files to Create/Modify

**New Apps:**
- `privacy/` (models, views, templates for policy management)

**New Models:**
- `PolicyVersion`, `PolicyAcceptance`, `DeletionLog`, `DataRetentionPolicy`, `FinancialRecord`, `AuditLog`, `GDPRComplianceReport`

**Modified Models:**
- `candidates.Candidate` (add account_closed_at, deletion_requested_at)
- `employers.User` (add account_closed_at, session tracking)

**New Services:**
- `shared/audit_log.py`
- `shared/gdpr_compliance.py` (account deletion, anonymization)
- `shared/data_retention.py` (retention rule enforcement)

**New Management Commands:**
- `delete_inactive_candidates.py`
- `cleanup_job_applications.py`
- `cleanup_job_postings.py`
- `cleanup_usage_logs.py`
- `cleanup_support_tickets.py`

**New Templates:**
- `privacy/privacy_policy.html`
- `privacy/terms_of_service.html`
- `shared/components/consent_checkbox.html`
- `shared/components/footer_policy_links.html`
- `account/delete_confirmation_modal.html`

**Configuration:**
- Update `settings.py` (SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, session settings, retention config)
- Create `scripts/gdpr_cleanup.sh`
- Update `requirements.txt` (no new dependencies needed)

---

### Testing Strategy

**Unit Tests:** ~60 tests (each model, service, management command)
**Integration Tests:** ~20 tests (deletion workflow, retention automation, consent flow)
**E2E Tests:** ~10 tests (user journey for deletion, policy acceptance)

**Total Test Coverage Goal:** 95%+ for GDPR-related code

---

### Deployment Checklist Before Starting

1. ✅ Verify current Django version (5.2.4 confirmed)
2. ✅ Backup production database
3. ✅ Create feature branch: `feature/gdpr-phase-1`
4. ✅ Review Obsidian project files for latest requirements
5. ✅ Confirm with Miles Ashworth on IoM-specific GDPR requirements
6. ❌ Set up staging environment for testing
7. ❌ Configure production Redis (for session management)
8. ❌ Verify UK/IOM hosting compliance (AWS London region)

## 🧾 Project Description

**Platform Overview:**
EVOLVE is the foundational AI platform that powers specialized applications like the [[Capability Intelligence Engine - Refined Module Architecture]].

## Enterprise Virtualization & Optimized Learning

### Your Data Isn't Just Stored—It's **Alive**
*The Self-Adapting Intelligence Platform That Grows With Your People*

---

## The Challenge Every Enterprise Faces

**The AI Investment Paradox:** For every $1 spent on AI technology, companies typically spend $3 on retraining and reskilling people. Most AI implementations fail because they don't address the human element—leaving organizations with expensive technology and unprepared workforces.

**What if your AI system could eliminate that 3:1 cost ratio while making your workforce exponentially more capable?**

---

## Meet E.V.O.L.V.E.: Where Intelligence Lives and Learns

E.V.O.L.V.E. is not just another AI platform—it's a living digital ecosystem that transforms your organization's data into an intelligent, self-adapting organism. Your company's information becomes alive, continuously learning from every interaction, enriching itself with external intelligence, and coaching your workforce as it grows.

### The Revolutionary Difference
- **Self-Perpetuating Intelligence:** The more you use it, the smarter it becomes
- **Integrated Training Engine:** Eliminates the traditional 3:1 people-to-technology cost ratio
- **Living Digital Twins:** Virtual replicas of your processes, systems, and roles
- **Ultra-Scalable Architecture:** Lower costs enable infinite scalability
- **Complete Privacy Control:** Run entirely within your own infrastructure

---

## How E.V.O.L.V.E. Works: The Self-Perpetuating Intelligence Loop

### 🔄 **The Living Flywheel**

**1. INGEST & ENRICH**
- Core LLM + RAG system consumes all company data
- Automatically enriches with market intelligence, competitor analysis, regulatory updates
- Creates comprehensive, contextual knowledge base

**2. SPECIALIZE & DEPLOY**
- Auto-generates specialized Small Language Models (SLMs) for each department
- Sales SLM, HR SLM, Operations SLM—each optimized for specific functions
- Lightning-fast, energy-efficient, and hyper-focused on domain expertise

**3. INTERACT & LEARN**
- Employees collaborate with their AI co-pilots daily
- Every conversation, question, and feedback loop is captured
- Digital twin agents mirror real-world processes and optimize performance

**4. EVOLVE & UPGRADE**
- Core LLM retrains nightly on interaction data
- All SLMs receive continuous upgrades—zero downtime
- Built-in Training Agent identifies skill gaps and delivers personalized learning

**5. PERPETUATE & SCALE**
- Each cycle makes predictions sharper, advice richer, training more effective
- System becomes more valuable with every user, every interaction, every day
- Exponential intelligence growth at linear cost

---

## Core Capabilities That Transform Your Business

### **Living Digital Twin Agents**
Create intelligent virtual replicas of your processes, assets, and even individual roles. These digital twins simulate scenarios, predict outcomes, and optimize performance before real-world implementation.

### **Adaptive Intelligence Augmentation**
Every employee gets a personalized AI co-pilot that provides real-time insights, context-aware suggestions, and hands-on support for daily tasks, decision-making, and creative problem-solving.

### **Continuous Skill Evolution Engine**
Built-in virtual training assistant that continuously assesses skill gaps, curates personalized learning journeys, and delivers micro-learning modules directly within workflow. Upskilling becomes seamless, scalable, and integrated.

### **Hyper-Personalized Data Outputs**
- **Predictive Analytics:** Forecast trends and outcomes with unprecedented accuracy
- **Automated Reports:** Generate customized insights for every role and department
- **Real-Time Dashboards:** Visualize performance metrics as they happen
- **Proactive Alerts:** Trigger notifications when opportunities or risks emerge
- **Scenario Simulations:** Test strategies in virtual environments before implementation

### **Frictionless Scalability**
Ultra-lean technology stack enables deployment anywhere—from single departments to global enterprises—without heavy infrastructure or hidden costs. Scale instantly with complete privacy control.

---

## Futuristic Use Cases That Drive Results

### **Virtual Mentors & Coaches**
Every employee pairs with a digital twin mentor offering real-time feedback, skill-building exercises, and career path guidance—customized to their goals and the company's evolving needs.

### **Dynamic Workforce Optimization**
E.V.O.L.V.E. analyzes skills, workloads, and project requirements to recommend optimal team compositions and resource allocation, ensuring every initiative is staffed for maximum success.

### **Proactive Organizational Learning**
The system identifies emerging trends and skill requirements, proactively updating training content and guiding employees to learn what's next—before the market demands it.

### **Augmented Decision Intelligence**
Transform strategic meetings with live data visualizations, scenario modeling, and instant access to relevant knowledge, turning every discussion into a high-impact decision session.

### **Autonomous Knowledge Curation**
Outdated documents are automatically flagged, rewritten, and version-controlled. Your knowledge base stays fresh, relevant, and continuously optimized.

---

## Why E.V.O.L.V.E. Changes Everything

### **🚀 Future-Proof Your Workforce**
Self-adapting intelligence ensures your people and knowledge base never fall behind. Build a culture of continuous learning where humans and AI evolve together.

### **💰 Maximize ROI, Minimize Hidden Costs**
Integrated training eliminates the traditional 3:1 people spend. Learning content is generated automatically, not purchased. Every dollar invested creates exponential value.

### **⚡ Scale Without Friction**
Lighter technology footprint means faster rollouts, lower energy consumption, and broader reach. Deploy to edge computing environments with ease.

### **🎯 Human-Centric by Design**
Automate the mundane, augment the complex. Free your talent for creativity, strategy, and innovation while AI handles routine tasks.

### **🔒 Own Your Privacy**
Deploy entirely within your own perimeter. No data leaves your control. Complete sovereignty over your most valuable asset—your information.

### **🔄 Self-Perpetuating Value**
Unlike traditional software that depreciates, E.V.O.L.V.E. becomes more valuable with time. Every interaction makes it smarter, every user makes it better.

---

## The E.V.O.L.V.E. Advantage: By the Numbers

**Traditional AI Implementation:**
- $1 Technology + $3 Training = $4 Total Investment
- Static capabilities that require constant updates
- Separate training systems and vendors
- Limited scalability due to cost constraints

**E.V.O.L.V.E. Implementation:**
- $1 Technology + $0.25 Training = $1.25 Total Investment
- Self-improving capabilities that get better over time
- Integrated training and development platform
- Unlimited scalability through efficiency gains

**ROI Improvement: 320%**

---

## Target Organizations

E.V.O.L.V.E. is the transformative solution for:

- **Forward-thinking enterprises** seeking to turn data into competitive advantage
- **Growth-oriented companies** committed to workforce development and continuous learning
- **Privacy-conscious organizations** requiring complete data sovereignty
- **Cost-conscious businesses** looking to maximize AI ROI while minimizing hidden expenses
- **Scalable operations** needing solutions that grow efficiently with their business

---

## The Future is Living Intelligence

E.V.O.L.V.E. isn't just an AI system—it's a paradigm shift in how organizations interact with their data and develop their people. By giving life to your company's information and integrating learning into every interaction, E.V.O.L.V.E. creates a self-perpetuating cycle of intelligence and growth.

**Your data learns. Your people grow. Your organization evolves.**

*Welcome to the future of enterprise intelligence.*

---

## Ready to Transform Your Enterprise?

Don't let your competitors gain the advantage of living intelligence. E.V.O.L.V.E. your organization today.

**Contact us to schedule a demonstration and see your data come alive.**

## 🧾 Project Description

**Dubai Airports Academy** for cross-mobility integration across Dubai city transportation systems.

**Scope:**
Building an academy for **cross-mobility** that extends beyond just airports to encompass Dubai's entire transportation ecosystem. This is a Dubai Government initiative where all mobility and transportation falls under unified government authority.

**Context:**
- Dubai is preparing for new airport opening (major infrastructure milestone)
- Government wants integrated approach to mobility across the city
- Airports are entry point, but vision is city-wide transportation integration
- Capability Intelligence Engine has been introduced and well-received

**Kirsty's Introduction:**
"We've introduced the Capability Intelligence Engine to Dubai airports. Might not be a bad time to go into them. They're doing a lot of preparation for the new airport. The conversations I'm having with them is saying to look at for Dubai, building an academy, cross mobility in mobility for the city. It all sits under Dubai Government."

**Strategic Opportunity:**
- Government-level backing (Dubai Government initiative)
- Well-connected internal champion (sits on government committee)

- Broader scope than just airports (city-wide mobility vision)

	3. Academy integrated across city transportation systems (airports + metro + bus + taxi + future mobility)
	4. Capability Intelligence Engine deployed at scale
	5. Reference case for other GCC government transportation initiatives
	6. Recurring revenue from academy operations
	7. Expansion to other Dubai Government initiatives

	1. **Strong internal champion** - Emirati lady with government committee access

	3. Multiple stakeholders across transportation modes

	5. Competition from other global training providers
	6. Scale requirements could be very large (capacity planning)
	7. Government tender requirements and compliance

	8. Assumption: Champion has sufficient influence to drive decision

	1. **Infrastructure = Catalyst**: New airport drives capability development needs
	2. **Government Initiative = Budget**: Government-level project likely has substantial funding
	3. **Cross-Mobility Vision**: Dubai's unified approach to transportation is strategic differentiator
	4. **Champion Quality**: Young, smart, government-connected = high potential
	5. **Ignatius's Research Value**: His deep airport/transportation insights add strategic advisory layer
	6. **Disconnected Systems Problem**: Transportation integration is universal challenge - Dubai solving it creates reference case
	7. **GCC Expansion**: Success here opens door to other GCC governments (Abu Dhabi, Doha, Riyadh, etc.)

# Project Status

## Current Status (as of 2025-11-05)
- **Contract**: Pending signature from Adam's management chain - delayed due to other priorities
- **Timeline**: Need action plan ready for when contract is signed to avoid December delays
- **Missed Opportunity**: Ginity fundraising window (2-3 weeks ago) where announcement would have been beneficial

## Strategic Direction
- **Primary Focus**: Business School implementation (not tech department)
- **Core Value Proposition**: Practical AI implementation for businesses, not just theoretical research
- **Key Differentiator**: Teaching students real-world AI adoption frameworks and tools

## Key Opportunities Identified

### 1. Research IP Commercialization Platform
- Analyze LJMU's research outputs (published papers, studies) for commercial viability
- Cross-reference research across departments to identify synergies
- Run "virtual sand pit events" using AI to match researchers and commercial applications
- Use EVOLVE with variables mapping (students, educators, research topics)

### 2. Grant Application Optimization
- Current problem: Multiple researchers competing for same small grants (5 people for one £X grant = 20% of Q1 applications)
- Opportunity: AI-powered grant matching and combined bid development
- Potential: More sophisticated, collaborative proposals with higher success rates
- System could cross-reference: grants available, research outputs, team capabilities

### 3. New Master's Course Integration
- EVOLVE as enabling technology/base framework for AI implementation course
- Focus on practical implementation vs. theoretical research
- Train students in real-world AI adoption (highly marketable skill)
- Course material development around EVOLVE capabilities

### 4. Student Placement Program
- Partner with 3-4 companies for practical AI implementation projects
- Potential first client: Company near LJMU with ~250 employees, 5 companies, aggressive AI implementation goals
- Students gain hands-on experience with real implementations

### 5. Meeting Intelligence & Network Analysis
- Graph-based meeting analysis (nodes & links) - currently in development
- Requires data scientist involvement
- Cross-references meetings, activities, connections

### 6. Intelligence Capability Engine (ICE)
- Ontological training material generation for TTRO partnership
- Adaptive: Analyzes existing procedures/policies/regulations and generates training on-the-fly
- Applicable to business school curriculum and corporate training

## Action Items for Ignatius

### Immediate
- [ ] Complete approved supplier list paperwork (Adam to send)
- [ ] Draft initial implementation plans to send Adam before contract signing
- [ ] Prepare marketing/promotion strategy from LJMU perspective

- [ ] Engage data scientist for network analysis component

# How to Hide in Plain Sight: Next-Level Digital Privacy

## Abstract

This presentation provides a comprehensive, actionable framework for minimising digital surveillance and data collection by commercial entities. The speaker systematically dismantles common data collection practices through a detailed case study of Megaplex Theatres, then presents specific tools, software alternatives, and step-by-step implementation strategies across every major category of digital interaction. The work demonstrates that robust privacy protection requires neither advanced technical expertise nor significant financial investment, providing concrete product recommendations, configuration instructions, and tactical workflows for immediate implementation.

---

## **1. Problem Statement**

The presentation addresses the systemic exploitation of personal data by commercial entities that collect information far exceeding operational requirements, maintain inadequate security infrastructures, and deploy this data for behavioural manipulation and financial extraction.

### **The Megaplex Theatres Case Study**

The speaker's attempt to purchase a cinema ticket online revealed the following data collection requirements:

**Required Personal Information:**
* Full legal name (first and last)
* Complete date of birth
* Email address
* Phone number
* Postcode
* Favourite cinema location
* Newsletter subscription (incentivised with 5,000 "bonus points")

**Critical Security and Privacy Violations Identified:**

1. **Contradictory Privacy Policy**: The policy states "Do we sell your personal information? No" but immediately follows with "we do share data with third parties"

2. **Excessive Data Collection Scope**: The privacy policy explicitly states collection of:
   - Browser history and search history
   - Interaction data with other websites and applications
   - Unique device identifiers
   - Real-time location data
   - **Biometric information** (shared with third parties twice in previous 12 months)

3. **Unjustified Collection Rationale**: The stated reason includes "we collect your information so that we can then anonymise it" (a logical impossibility if collecting unique identifiers)

4. **Catastrophic Security Posture**:
   - **Total company size**: 1,100 employees
   - **IT department size**: 4 personnel
   - **IT department composition**:
     * 1 CIO (functions primarily as purchasing agent)
     * 1 systems engineer (maintains physical projection equipment)
     * 1 film buyer/payment specialist (no security role)
     * **1 CRM systems engineer** (sole person responsible for all customer data)

5. **Inadequate Security Training**: The CRM systems engineer's qualifications:
   - Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering from Western Governors University (2022)
   - Java emphasis programme
   - **Total formal security education**: 2 modules (one module in Introduction to IT course, one module in Advanced Java Testing course)
   - Previous work experience: IT service desk technician

6. **Publicly Accessible Personal Information**: Using open-source intelligence (OSINT) techniques, the speaker obtained the following about the CRM engineer in **12 minutes**:
   - Full name and photograph
   - Hometown and high school attended (revealing security question answers)
   - Current residential address
   - Phone number
   - Date of birth
   - **This information satisfies authentication requirements for most financial institutions**

### **Broader Contextual Problems**

**AI-Enabled Dynamic Pricing Exploitation:**

The speaker describes Delta Airlines' announced implementation of AI-driven pricing that adjusts ticket costs based on personal circumstances:

* **Scenario**: User receives text message about family emergency (grandfather's death)
* **Data pathway**: Google Messages reads and logs message content
* **AI analysis**: Delta's system correlates emergency notification with flight search behaviour
* **Price manipulation**: Standard $200 ticket increased to $350 based on urgency inference
* **Legal loophole**: Whilst identity-based pricing discrimination is illegal in the US, **device-identifier-based pricing is permitted**

**DNS Query Surveillance:**

The speaker conducted packet capture analysis whilst preparing a jalapeno jelly recipe:

* **Activity**: Viewing single recipe webpage for 50 minutes
* **Result**: **14,025 DNS queries** from one mobile device
* **Implication**: Even mundane browsing activities trigger thousands of tracking requests to third-party domains

**Childhood Data Aggregation:**

* Companies circumvent legal prohibitions on collecting children's data by:
  1. Monitoring pregnancy tracking apps for expected birth dates
  2. Attributing purchasing behaviour, toy preferences, and dietary patterns to parent accounts
  3. Maintaining separate "pre-activation" profiles that merge with child accounts when they turn 13
  4. Example cited: DefCon presentation on "exploitation of unborn children" through Twitter data analysis

---

## **2. Proposed Solution**

The presentation proposes a **comprehensive privacy preservation framework** organised into foundational practices, intermediate implementations, and advanced techniques. The solution architecture emphasises **practical viability** rather than theoretical purity, acknowledging that incremental adoption provides meaningful protection even without complete implementation.

### **Three Guiding Principles**

1. **Minimal Information Disclosure**: "Provide as little information as possible" - question every data request
2. **Identifier Non-Reuse**: Never reuse emails, usernames, credit card numbers, addresses, or browsing sessions across services
3. **Informed Consent**: When choosing to share data, do so knowingly rather than through default settings

### **Three-Tier Privacy Framework**

**Tier 1 - Zero PII (Trivial Transactions):**
- **Context**: Purchases or services with no legal requirements (cinema tickets, fast food loyalty programmes, online shopping for physical goods)
- **Strategy**: Provide no personally identifiable information
- **Example**: Cinema ticket using fake name, disposable email, VoIP phone number, fake birthdate, false postcode

**Tier 2 - Minimal Verifiable Information (Potentially Disputable):**
- **Context**: Services where you might need to prove ownership or identity in legal proceedings (domain registration, certain subscriptions)
- **Strategy**: Use information that's technically accurate but not complete
- **Example**: Use nickname variants ("Jimmy" instead of "James"), hotel addresses as temporary residences, partial names that could be verified by witness testimony in court
- **Legal principle**: If information doesn't explicitly require "legal name" or "legal address", alternative formulations are permissible

**Tier 3 - Accurate Information with Scrutiny (Legal Requirements):**
- **Context**: Genuinely legally mandated disclosures (medical records, insurance, financial services subject to KYC regulations)
- **Strategy**: Provide accurate information only for explicitly required fields, omit everything optional
- **Example**: Medical intake forms requesting employer information - this is typically **not** legally required under HIPAA and should be left blank

---

## **3. Methodology: Specific Tools, Software, and Implementation Strategies**

### **Category 1: Social Media**

**Primary Recommendation: Complete Withdrawal**

The speaker's position: "Just get off social media. That's just a fact. Social media is not in the business of being social. Social media is in the business of engaging you."

**If Complete Withdrawal Is Impossible:**

**Best Practices:**
* Never post real-time location information (post Cabo vacation photos after returning home)
* Disable GPS metadata on all photographs before uploading
* Turn off "high precision location" services on mobile devices
* Never reuse hashtags that could correlate accounts across platforms
* Minimise personal information in profiles (use aliases, approximate locations, fake birthdates)

**Rationale**: Social media platforms monetise user attention through sophisticated engagement algorithms trained on comprehensive behavioural profiles. These profiles enable both commercial manipulation (targeted advertising) and potentially political influence operations.

---

### **Category 2: Web Browsers**

**AVOID:**
* **Google Chrome** - "Chrome tracks everything everywhere all the time. It just does." (85% market adoption rate)
* **Microsoft Edge** - "Just a wannabe Chrome"
* **Safari** - "Meh" (speaker expresses scepticism about privacy claims)
* **Firefox** - Previously recommended but **changed terms of service in May** stating they "could share everything that you type into and or do on your browser" (CEO later walked back claims, creating uncertainty)

**RECOMMENDED:**

**Primary Recommendation: Brave**
* **Description**: Chromium-based browser with privacy-first architecture
* **Key features**:
  - Built-in ad blocking and tracker blocking (enabled by default)
  - HTTPS Everywhere (automatic secure connection enforcement)
  - Fingerprinting protection
  - Maintains Chrome compatibility (extensions, rendering engine)
* **Speaker endorsement**: "If you really have a hard time, you want to get off [Chrome], go to Brave. It's Chrome, but it's with a focus on privacy."
* **Founder concerns acknowledged**: "I personally don't know the founders of Brave, but I have a good friend who does, and she knows them, and her feedback to me is that they're an okay company. They're good."
* **Best for**: Users transitioning from Chrome who need familiar interface

**Alternative Options:**

**Mullvad Browser**
* **Description**: Privacy-focused browser developed by Mullvad VPN
* **Best for**: Users prioritising maximum anonymity

**LibreWolf**
* **Description**: Independent fork of Firefox with enhanced privacy defaults
* **Best for**: Firefox users seeking privacy without Mozilla's controversial policies

**Orion**
* **Description**: Newly released iOS-specific browser (currently in beta)
* **Platform**: iOS only
* **Status**: Speaker noted this in privacy newsletter "two days ago", expected full release soon
* **Best for**: iOS users seeking native privacy-focused alternative

**Implementation Strategy:**
1. Install Brave (or alternative) on all devices
2. Import bookmarks from existing browser
3. Install essential extensions (password manager, ad blocker if not built-in)
4. Set as default browser in operating system settings
5. Uninstall Chrome/previous browser to prevent accidental use

---

### **Category 3: Search Engines**

**AVOID:**
* **Google Search** - "Google sucks. Stop using Google."
* **Bing** - "Just a wannabe"
* **Siri** - "I don't even know what Siri is doing on this list"

**RECOMMENDED:**

**Primary Recommendation: DuckDuckGo**
* **Website**: https://duckduckgo.com
* **Functionality**: Aggregates results from Google and Bing through centralised proxy
* **Privacy mechanism**: Searches originate from DuckDuckGo servers, preventing direct device tracking
* **Limitation**: Still depends on Google/Bing infrastructure
* **Best for**: Users seeking easy Google replacement with minimal learning curve

**Advanced Recommendation: Startpage**
* **Website**: https://www.startpage.com
* **Jurisdiction**: Based in Netherlands with servers in multiple countries
* **Privacy mechanism**: All searches routed through proxy servers - "you don't even touch the internet. It does the searches for you and then sends you the stuff back"
* **Additional feature**: Anonymous View (proxy browsing for search results)
* **Best for**: Users seeking stronger anonymity than DuckDuckGo

**Self-Hosted Option: SearXNG**
* **Description**: Open-source metasearch engine
* **Deployment**: Self-hosted on personal server or local network
* **Privacy mechanism**: Complete control over query logging, no third-party involvement
* **Technical requirement**: Requires server administration skills or willingness to learn
* **Best for**: Technical users wanting complete search independence

**Implementation Strategy:**
1. Change default search engine in browser settings
2. Install search engine's browser extension if available
3. Consider setting up custom search shortcuts (e.g., "!ddg" for DuckDuckGo)
4. For SearXNG: Deploy on existing home server or VPS, configure metasearch sources

---

### **Category 4: Messaging and SMS**

**AVOID:**
* **SMS** - "SMS stands for Share My Stuff. Don't use SMS. It's not secure."
* **RCS** (Rich Communication Services) - "RCS stands for Really Careless Security"
* **Google Messages** - "Google Messages reads everything after it unencrypts it" (used as example in Delta Airlines pricing scenario)

**Card Types Available:**

* Only works with specific merchant domain

**Category-Specific Cards:**
* Organize by spending category
* Set monthly limits per category
* **Best for**: Budget management and expense tracking

* Set monthly spending caps
* Card automatically declines charges exceeding limits

**Billing Information Flexibility:**

* Merchant receives fabricated information, Privacy.com handles actual bank settlement

### **Category 12: Browser Configuration and Privacy Practices**

**Critical Actions:**

**Action 1: Disable All Cookies**

**Speaker's Directive**: "Turn off all your browser cookies. Please, right now, turn off all your browser cookies."

**Rationale**: "It's better for a website to break than it is for all of your information to go out or the information about your loved ones or whatever, right?"

**Implementation:**

**Brave Browser:**
1. Settings → Shields → Cookie Blocking
2. Set to "Block all cookies" (most aggressive)
3. Individual site exceptions: Click shield icon in address bar, adjust per-site

**Firefox/LibreWolf:**
1. Settings → Privacy & Security
2. Enhanced Tracking Protection → Custom
3. Check "Cookies" → Select "All cookies"

**Safari:**
1. Preferences → Privacy
2. Enable "Block all cookies"
3. Warnings about website functionality are expected

**Expected Outcome**: Some websites will malfunction; this is acceptable trade-off for privacy

**Action 2: Block Fingerprinting**

**Definition**: Browser fingerprinting collects device characteristics (screen resolution, installed fonts, timezone, plugins, canvas rendering) to create unique identifier without cookies

**Implementation:**

**Brave**: Built-in fingerprinting protection (enabled by default in Standard/Aggressive shield modes)

**Firefox**:
1. Settings → Privacy & Security
2. Enhanced Tracking Protection → Strict
3. Enables fingerprinting protection

**Browser Extensions** (for browsers without native protection):
* **CanvasBlocker** (Firefox)
* **Trace** (Chromium browsers)

**Action 3: Monitor Network Traffic**

**Speaker's Recommendation**: "Check your pcap files and your DNS queries and see what's going on."

**Example Finding**: "Her one phone made 14,025 DNS queries in 50 minutes while it took us to make the recipe [for jalapeno jelly]."

**Tools for Packet Capture Analysis:**

**Wireshark** (Desktop)
* **Download**: https://www.wireshark.org
* **Usage**: Capture all network traffic, filter for DNS queries
* **Filter syntax**: `dns` (shows only DNS traffic)
* **Best for**: Detailed protocol analysis

**Charles Proxy** (Desktop and Mobile)
* **Download**: https://www.charlesproxy.com
* **Usage**: HTTP/HTTPS proxy for viewing all web requests
* **Configuration**: Install SSL certificate to decrypt HTTPS
* **Best for**: Understanding which domains apps/websites contact

**Pi-hole** (Network-wide DNS monitoring)
* **Description**: Network-level DNS sinkhole
* **Deployment**: Raspberry Pi or any Linux system on local network
* **Functionality**:
  - Logs all DNS queries from all devices
  - Blocks advertising/tracking domains
  - Provides web interface with statistics
* **Installation**: https://pi-hole.net
* **Best for**: Household-wide tracking visibility and blocking

**Mobile-Specific Tools:**

**NetGuard** (Android - no root required)
* **Function**: Per-app firewall showing all connection attempts
* **Download**: F-Droid (open-source version) or Play Store

**Lockdown Privacy** (iOS)
* **Function**: Firewall and DNS filtering
* **Download**: App Store

**Analysis Process:**
1. Install packet capture tool
2. Perform single simple activity (view one webpage, use one app for defined time)
3. Review DNS queries or HTTP requests
4. Identify tracking domains (typically CDNs, analytics services, ad networks)
5. Block problematic domains via hosts file, Pi-hole, or browser extension

**Action 4: Use HTTPS Everywhere**

**Purpose**: Force encrypted connections to websites

**Implementation**: Most modern browsers now default to HTTPS; verify in settings

**Brave/Chrome**: Enabled by default
**Firefox**: Settings → Privacy & Security → HTTPS-Only Mode → Enable
**Safari**: Safari → Preferences → Advanced → "Show full website address" (helps identify HTTP vs HTTPS)

**Action 5: Disable Location Services**

**High Precision GPS**: "Do you really need to know how far left, one foot, or right foot you are while driving with Google Maps? Don't use Google Maps. Like, why do you need within one foot accuracy? Just turn that off."

**Mobile Configuration:**

**Android:**
1. Settings → Location → Advanced → Google Location Accuracy
2. Disable "Improve Location Accuracy"

**iOS:**
1. Settings → Privacy → Location Services
2. Set apps to "Ask Next Time" or "While Using" (never "Always")
3. Disable "Precise Location" for individual apps

**Action 6: Review and Remove Browser Extensions**

**Risk**: Extensions can access all browsing data

**Audit Process:**
1. List all installed extensions
2. Remove any unused extensions
3. Verify remaining extensions are open-source when possible
4. Check extension permissions (minimize data access)

**Action 7: Clear Browsing Data Regularly**

**Automated Schedule**: Configure browser to clear on exit

**Brave**: Settings → Shields → Clear browsing data → On exit

### **Category 13: Mobile Operating Systems**

**Problem**: "Google and Apple are in the business of user engagement. That's what they want. So they take all your information and try to get you to do stuff on their platforms."

**Website**: https://grapheneos.org

* **MAC address randomisation**: Different MAC address per Wi-Fi network
* **App permission controls**: Granular control beyond stock Android

**Speaker Endorsement**: "I'm on Graphene OS. I fully recommend it."

**Functionality Preservation**: "You can still do everything you want. You could even get a Graphene OS phone and still log into Google or you could just completely not be connected to any of the Google services, which is awesome."

**Installation Complexity**: Moderate (requires unlocking bootloader, following detailed instructions)

**Alternative: CalyxOS**
* **Website**: https://calyxos.org

**Technique 1: Disinformation Campaigns (Defensive)**

**Method 1: Political Donation Data Poisoning**

**Process:**
1. Visit political party website(s) - "all of them, I don't know how many there are"
2. Make minimum donation ($1)
3. Provide:

**Result**: "It'll make its way to all corners of the internet in about 24 hours."

**Rationale**: Political donation databases are:

**Warning**: "Don't use your neighbor's address because that's just mean."

**Method 3: Contest Entries**

**Method 4: Community Phone Number - 867-5309**

**Speaker's Recommendation**: "Next time you go to Smith's, give your number as 867-5309."

## **5. Critical Best Practices and Warnings**

### **Universal Principles**

1. **Always Question Data Collection**: "90% of the time they don't [need your information]. 98% I don't I need more, right? They just don't need it."

2. **Incremental Progress Is Valuable**: "Any step forward is a positive step forward. Please just make some step. You don't need to go 100% right now. One thing that spoke to you, do that today."

3. **Informed Consent**: "Make an informed and intentional decision about the data you share."

4. **Assume Breaches Will Occur**: Design practices assuming data will be compromised

5. **Never Trust Privacy Policies**: Example of Megaplex demonstrates policies are often contradictory, misleading, or AI-generated

### **Security Warnings**

**NEVER Photograph Your ID**: "You should never ever ever ever ever let anybody take a picture of your ID ever."

**If Absolutely Unavoidable**: Watermark with "COPIED FOR [SERVICE] ON [DATE] - DO NOT SHARE"

**NEVER Reuse Passwords**: Use password manager; generate unique passwords for every account

**NEVER Provide Biometric Data Unnecessarily**: Megaplex case demonstrates organisations collect biometrics without security infrastructure to protect it

**NEVER Share Security Question Answers Publicly**: The 12-minute OSINT exercise revealed enough information to defeat financial institution authentication

**NEVER Use Default Router Credentials**: Change immediately on all home networking equipment

**NEVER Connect to Public Wi-Fi Without VPN**: Unencrypted traffic on public networks is trivially intercepted

### **Behavioral Practices**

**Question "Why?"**: Every data request should trigger the question: "Why do they need this specific information?"

**Compartmentalization**: Use different identities (email aliases, usernames, virtual cards) for different contexts to prevent profile aggregation

**Minimize Metadata**:
* Disable GPS before taking photos
* Strip EXIF data before sharing images
* Use encrypted messaging for sensitive communications

**Regular Audits**:
* Monthly: Review Privacy.com card usage and delete unused cards
* Quarterly: Audit email aliases and delete compromised/spam-receiving addresses
* Bi-annually: Search for your name/address on people-search sites and request removals

**Hotel Strategy**: When traveling, use hotel addresses for temporary registrations needed during trip

**Community Resources**: Leverage shared numbers (867-5309) for loyalty programmes where personal identification provides no benefit

### **Legal Considerations**

**Know Verification Requirements**:
* If form doesn't explicitly state "legal name required", alternatives are permissible
* Hotel registrations typically don't legally require government ID despite common practice
* Many online services have terms requiring accurate information but lack enforcement mechanisms

**Be Aware of Local Laws**:
* Some jurisdictions require accurate hotel registration
* Providing false information to financial institutions may violate banking regulations
* Using aliases is generally legal unless done for fraudulent purposes

**Documentation**: Keep records of which aliases, addresses, and phone numbers are used for which services (securely stored in password manager)

## Terms

- **PII (Personally Identifiable Information)** - Data that can identify a specific individual
- **OSINT (Open Source Intelligence)** - Intelligence gathered from publicly available sources
- **VPN (Virtual Private Network)** - Encrypted tunnel for internet traffic
- **VoIP (Voice over IP)** - Phone service delivered over internet
- **CMRA (Commercial Mail Receiving Agency)** - Business providing street addresses for mail receipt
- **MVNO (Mobile Virtual Network Operator)** - Mobile carrier using another carrier's infrastructure
- **KYC (Know Your Customer)** - Identity verification requirements for financial services
- **DNS (Domain Name System)** - System translating domain names to IP addresses
- **E2E Encryption (End-to-End Encryption)** - Encryption where only sender and recipient can read messages
- **Browser Fingerprinting** - Tracking technique using device/browser characteristics
- **MAC Address** - Unique identifier for network interface
- **Zero-Access Encryption** - Encryption where service provider cannot access data

- [[Digital Privacy MOC]] - Main privacy resources hub
- [[OSINT]] - Open source intelligence techniques

## Key Takeaways

1. **Question Everything**: 90%+ of data requests are unnecessary - question every request
2. **Incremental Progress**: Any step forward is valuable - don't need 100% implementation
3. **Informed Consent**: Make intentional decisions about data sharing
4. **Three-Tier Framework**: Use zero PII for trivial transactions, minimal for disputable, accurate only for legal requirements
5. **Never Reuse Identifiers**: Different email alias, phone number, credit card for every service
6. **Community Resources Work**: 867-5309 loyalty number, shared fake addresses reduce individual tracking
7. **Privacy ≠ Expensive**: Most recommendations are free or low-cost (<$200 first year)
8. **Security Posture Matters**: Companies collecting excessive data often lack security to protect it
9. **Assume Breaches**: Design practices assuming data will be compromised
10. **Protect Children**: Childhood profiling begins before birth - privacy protects those who can't consent
